Whilst there are no formal concordats between the Scottish Government, Welsh Government and Northern Ireland Executive, ministers from each devolved government meet at various points throughout the year at various events such as the British-Irish Council and also meet to discuss matters and issues that are devolved to each government.<sup id="cite_ref-gov.scot_221-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-gov.scot-221">&#91;221&#93;</a></sup> Scotland, along with the Welsh Government, British Government as well as the Northern Ireland executive, participate in the Joint Ministerial Committee (JMC) which allows each government to discuss policy issues together and work together across each government to find solutions. The Scottish Government considers the successful re-establishment of the Plenary, and establishment of the Domestic fora to be important facets of the relationship with the British Government and the other devolved administrations.<sup id="cite_ref-gov.scot_221-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-gov.scot-221">&#91;221&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In the aftermath of the United Kingdom's decision to withdraw from the European Union in 2016, the Scottish Government has called for there to be a joint approach from each of the devolved governments. In early 2017, the devolved governments met to discuss Brexit and agree on Brexit strategies from each devolved government<sup id="cite_ref-222" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-222">&#91;222&#93;</a></sup> which lead for <a href="/wiki/Theresa_May" title="Theresa May">Theresa May</a> to issue a statement that stated that the devolved governments will not have a central role or decision-making process in the Brexit process, but that the central government plans to "fully engage" Scotland in talks alongside the governments of Wales and Northern Ireland.<sup id="cite_ref-223" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-223">&#91;223&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="International_diplomacy">International diplomacy</span></h3>
<div class="thumb tleft"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:192px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Bush%26McConnell.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1a/Bush%26McConnell.jpg/190px-Bush%26McConnell.jpg" decoding="async" width="190" height="296" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1a/Bush%26McConnell.jpg/285px-Bush%26McConnell.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1a/Bush%26McConnell.jpg/380px-Bush%26McConnell.jpg 2x" data-file-width="515" data-file-height="802" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Bush%26McConnell.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>First Minister <a href="/wiki/Jack_McConnell" title="Jack McConnell">Jack McConnell</a> greets U.S. President <a href="/wiki/George_W._Bush" title="George W. Bush">George W. Bush</a> ahead of the <a href="/wiki/31st_G8_summit" title="31st G8 summit">31st G8 summit</a>, July 2005.</div></div></div>
<p>Whilst foreign policy remains a reserved matter,<sup id="cite_ref-224" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-224">&#91;224&#93;</a></sup> the Scottish Government may promote the economy and Scottish interests on the world stage and encourage foreign businesses, international devolved, regional and central governments to invest in Scotland.<sup id="cite_ref-225" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-225">&#91;225&#93;</a></sup> Whilst the first minister usually undertakes a number of foreign and international visits to promote Scotland, international relations, European and Commonwealth relations are also included within the portfolios of both the <a href="/wiki/Cabinet_Secretary_for_Culture,_Tourism_and_External_Affairs" class="mw-redirect" title="Cabinet Secretary for Culture, Tourism and External Affairs">Cabinet Secretary for Culture, Tourism and External Affairs</a> (responsible for international development)<sup id="cite_ref-226" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-226">&#91;226&#93;</a></sup> and the <a href="/wiki/Minister_for_International_Development_and_Europe" class="mw-redirect" title="Minister for International Development and Europe">Minister for International Development and Europe</a> (responsible for European Union relations and international relations).<sup id="cite_ref-227" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-227">&#91;227&#93;</a></sup> Scotland has been represented as a separate entity on some occasions at international organisations such as the <a href="/wiki/Nordic_Council" title="Nordic Council">Nordic Council</a> and the <a href="/wiki/United_Nations" title="United Nations">United Nations</a>. <sup id="cite_ref-228" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-228">&#91;228&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-229" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-229">&#91;229&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-230" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-230">&#91;230&#93;</a></sup> 
</p><p>Whilst an independent sovereign nation, Scotland had a close "special relationship" with <a href="/wiki/France" title="France">France</a> (known then as the <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_France" title="Kingdom of France">Kingdom of France</a>). In 1295, both Scotland and France signed what became known as the <a href="/wiki/Auld_Alliance" title="Auld Alliance">Auld Alliance</a> in <a href="/wiki/Paris" title="Paris">Paris</a>, which acted as a military and diplomatic alliance between English invasion and expansion.<sup id="cite_ref-bbc.co.uk_231-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-bbc.co.uk-231">&#91;231&#93;</a></sup> The French military sought the assistance of Scotland in 1415 during the <a href="/wiki/Battle_of_Agincourt" title="Battle of Agincourt">Battle of Agincourt</a> which was close to bringing the Kingdom of France to collapse.<sup id="cite_ref-bbc.co.uk_231-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-bbc.co.uk-231">&#91;231&#93;</a></sup> The Auld Alliance was seen as important for Scotland and its position within Europe, having signed a treaty of military, economic and diplomatic co-operation with a wealthy European nation.<sup id="cite_ref-232" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-232">&#91;232&#93;</a></sup> There had been an agreement between Scotland and France that allowed citizens of both countries to hold dual citizenship, which was revoked by the French Government in 1903.<sup id="cite_ref-233" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-233">&#91;233&#93;</a></sup> In recent times, there have been arguments that indicate that the Auld Alliance was never formally ended by either Scotland or France, and that many elements of the treaty may remain in place today.<sup id="cite_ref-234" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-234">&#91;234&#93;</a></sup> Scotland and France still have a special relationship, with a Statement of Intent being signed in 2013 which committed both Scotland and France to building on shared history, friendship, co-operation between governments and cultural exchange programmes.<sup id="cite_ref-235" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-235">&#91;235&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Nicola_Sturgeon_meets_Icelandic_Prime_Minister,_Katr%C3%ADn_Jakobsd%C3%B3ttir.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cd/Nicola_Sturgeon_meets_Icelandic_Prime_Minister%2C_Katr%C3%ADn_Jakobsd%C3%B3ttir.jpg/220px-Nicola_Sturgeon_meets_Icelandic_Prime_Minister%2C_Katr%C3%ADn_Jakobsd%C3%B3ttir.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="145" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cd/Nicola_Sturgeon_meets_Icelandic_Prime_Minister%2C_Katr%C3%ADn_Jakobsd%C3%B3ttir.jpg/330px-Nicola_Sturgeon_meets_Icelandic_Prime_Minister%2C_Katr%C3%ADn_Jakobsd%C3%B3ttir.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/c/cd/Nicola_Sturgeon_meets_Icelandic_Prime_Minister%2C_Katr%C3%ADn_Jakobsd%C3%B3ttir.jpg/440px-Nicola_Sturgeon_meets_Icelandic_Prime_Minister%2C_Katr%C3%ADn_Jakobsd%C3%B3ttir.jpg 2x" data-file-width="6031" data-file-height="3976" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Nicola_Sturgeon_meets_Icelandic_Prime_Minister,_Katr%C3%ADn_Jakobsd%C3%B3ttir.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>First Minister Sturgeon meets with <a href="/wiki/Katr%C3%ADn_Jakobsd%C3%B3ttir" title="Katrín Jakobsdóttir">Katrín Jakobsdóttir</a>, <a href="/wiki/Prime_Minister_of_Iceland" title="Prime Minister of Iceland">Prime Minister of Iceland</a>, 2019.</div></div></div>
<p>During the <a href="/wiki/31st_G8_summit" title="31st G8 summit">31st G8 summit</a> in 2005, the first minister of Scotland <a href="/wiki/Jack_McConnell" title="Jack McConnell">Jack McConnell</a> welcomed each head of government of the G8 nations to the country's <a href="/wiki/Glasgow_Prestwick_Airport" title="Glasgow Prestwick Airport">Glasgow Prestwick Airport</a><sup id="cite_ref-236" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-236">&#91;236&#93;</a></sup> on behalf of prime minister <a href="/wiki/Tony_Blair" title="Tony Blair">Tony Blair</a>. At the same time, McConnell and the then Scottish Executive pioneered the way forward to launch what would become the <a href="/wiki/Scotland_Malawi_Partnership" title="Scotland Malawi Partnership">Scotland Malawi Partnership</a> which co-ordinates Scottish activities to strengthen existing links with <a href="/wiki/Malawi" title="Malawi">Malawi</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-237" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-237">&#91;237&#93;</a></sup> During McConnell's time as first minister, several relations with Scotland, including Scottish and Russian relations strengthened following a visit by <a href="/wiki/President_of_Russia" title="President of Russia">President of Russia</a> <a href="/wiki/Vladimir_Putin" title="Vladimir Putin">Vladimir Putin</a> to <a href="/wiki/Edinburgh" title="Edinburgh">Edinburgh</a>. McConnell, speaking at the end, highlighted that the visit by Putin was a "post-devolution" step towards "Scotland regaining its international identity".<sup id="cite_ref-238" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-238">&#91;238&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Under the Salmond administration, Scotland's trade and investment deals with countries such as China<sup id="cite_ref-239" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-239">&#91;239&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-240" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-240">&#91;240&#93;</a></sup> and Canada, where Salmond established the Canada Plan 2010–2015 which aimed to strengthen "the important historical, cultural and economic links" between both Canada and Scotland.<sup id="cite_ref-241" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-241">&#91;241&#93;</a></sup> To promote Scotland's interests and Scottish businesses in North America, there is a Scottish Affairs Office located in <a href="/wiki/Washington,_D.C." title="Washington, D.C.">Washington, D.C.</a> with the aim to promoting Scotland in both the United States and Canada.<sup id="cite_ref-242" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-242">&#91;242&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>During a 2017 visit to the United States, the first minister Nicola Sturgeon met <a href="/wiki/Jerry_Brown" title="Jerry Brown">Jerry Brown</a>, <a href="/wiki/Governor_of_California" title="Governor of California">Governor of California</a>, where both signed an agreement committing both the Government of California and the Scottish Government to work together to tackle <a href="/wiki/Climate_change" title="Climate change">climate change</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-243" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-243">&#91;243&#93;</a></sup> as well as Sturgeon signing a £6.3&#160;million deal for Scottish investment from American businesses and firms promoting trade, tourism and innovation.<sup id="cite_ref-244" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-244">&#91;244&#93;</a></sup> During an official visit to the <a href="/wiki/Republic_of_Ireland" title="Republic of Ireland">Republic of Ireland</a> in 2016, Sturgeon stated that is it "important for Ireland and Scotland and the whole of the British Isles that Ireland has a strong ally in Scotland".<sup id="cite_ref-firstminister.gov.scot_245-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-firstminister.gov.scot-245">&#91;245&#93;</a></sup> During the same engagement, Sturgeon became the first head of government to address the <a href="/wiki/Seanad_%C3%89ireann" title="Seanad Éireann">Seanad Éireann</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Upper_house" title="Upper house">upper house</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Oireachtas" title="Oireachtas">Oireachtas</a> (the Irish parliament).<sup id="cite_ref-firstminister.gov.scot_245-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-firstminister.gov.scot-245">&#91;245&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h4><span class="mw-headline" id="International_Offices">International Offices</span></h4>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Henry_McLeish_and_George_W._Bush_in_the_Oval_Office,_2001.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/19/Henry_McLeish_and_George_W._Bush_in_the_Oval_Office%2C_2001.jpg/220px-Henry_McLeish_and_George_W._Bush_in_the_Oval_Office%2C_2001.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="126" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/1/19/Henry_McLeish_and_George_W._Bush_in_the_Oval_Office%2C_2001.jpg 1.5x" data-file-width="315" data-file-height="180" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Henry_McLeish_and_George_W._Bush_in_the_Oval_Office,_2001.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>First Minister <a href="/wiki/Henry_McLeish" title="Henry McLeish">Henry McLeish</a> meets <a href="/wiki/President_of_the_United_States" title="President of the United States">US President</a> <a href="/wiki/George_W._Bush" title="George W. Bush">George W. Bush</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Oval_Office" title="Oval Office">Oval Office</a> of the <a href="/wiki/White_House" title="White House">White House</a>, April 2001.</div></div></div>
<p>Scotland has a network of eight international offices across the world, these are located in:
</p>
<ul><li><a href="/wiki/Beijing" title="Beijing">Beijing</a> (Scottish Government Beijing Office) (<a href="/wiki/List_of_diplomatic_missions_of_the_United_Kingdom" title="List of diplomatic missions of the United Kingdom">British Embassy</a>)</li>
<li><a href="/wiki/Berlin" title="Berlin">Berlin</a> (Scottish Government Berlin Office)</li>
<li><a href="/wiki/Brussels" title="Brussels">Brussels</a> (Scotland House Brussels)</li>
<li><a href="/wiki/Copenhagen" title="Copenhagen">Copenhagen</a> (Scottish Government Copenhagen Office)<sup id="cite_ref-246" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-246">&#91;246&#93;</a></sup></li>
<li><a href="/wiki/Dublin" title="Dublin">Dublin</a> (Scottish Government Dublin Office) (British Embassy)</li>
<li><a href="/wiki/London" title="London">London</a> (Scotland House London)</li>
<li><a href="/wiki/Ottawa" title="Ottawa">Ottawa</a> (Scottish Government Ottawa Office) (British High Commission)</li>
<li><a href="/wiki/Paris" title="Paris">Paris</a> (Scottish Government Office) (British Embassy)</li>
<li><a href="/wiki/Washington,_D.C." title="Washington, D.C.">Washington DC</a> (Scottish Government Washington DC Office) (British Embassy)<sup id="cite_ref-247" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-247">&#91;247&#93;</a></sup></li></ul>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Constitutional_changes">Constitutional changes</span></h3>
<div class="thumb tleft"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Donald_Dour_(11570650893).jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/eb/Donald_Dour_%2811570650893%29.jpg/220px-Donald_Dour_%2811570650893%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="146" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/eb/Donald_Dour_%2811570650893%29.jpg/330px-Donald_Dour_%2811570650893%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/eb/Donald_Dour_%2811570650893%29.jpg/440px-Donald_Dour_%2811570650893%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4288" data-file-height="2848" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Donald_Dour_(11570650893).jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div><a href="/wiki/Donald_Dewar" title="Donald Dewar">Donald Dewar</a>, the first <a href="/wiki/First_Minister_of_Scotland" title="First Minister of Scotland">First Minister of Scotland</a>, is often regarded as the <i>Father of the Nation</i>.<sup id="cite_ref-248" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-248">&#91;248&#93;</a></sup></div></div></div>
<p>A policy of <a href="/wiki/Devolution" title="Devolution">devolution</a> had been advocated by the three main British political parties with varying enthusiasm during recent history. A previous Labour leader, <a href="/wiki/John_Smith_(Labour_Party_leader)" title="John Smith (Labour Party leader)">John Smith</a>, described the revival of a Scottish parliament as the "settled will of the Scottish people".<sup id="cite_ref-249" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-249">&#91;249&#93;</a></sup> The devolved Scottish Parliament was created after a <a href="/wiki/Scottish_devolution_referendum,_1997" class="mw-redirect" title="Scottish devolution referendum, 1997">referendum in 1997</a> found majority support for both creating the Parliament and granting it limited powers to <a href="/wiki/Scottish_variable_rate" title="Scottish variable rate">vary income tax</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-250" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-250">&#91;250&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The Scottish National Party (SNP), which supports <a href="/wiki/Scottish_independence" title="Scottish independence">Scottish independence</a>, was first elected to form the Scottish Government in <a href="/wiki/Scottish_Parliament_general_election,_2007" class="mw-redirect" title="Scottish Parliament general election, 2007">2007</a>. The new government established a "<a href="/wiki/National_Conversation" title="National Conversation">National Conversation</a>" on constitutional issues, proposing a number of options such as increasing the powers of the Scottish Parliament, <a href="/wiki/Federation" title="Federation">federalism</a>, or a referendum on Scottish independence from the United Kingdom. In rejecting the last option, the three main opposition parties in the Scottish Parliament created a <a href="/wiki/Calman_Commission" class="mw-redirect" title="Calman Commission">commission</a> to investigate the distribution of powers between devolved Scottish and UK-wide bodies.<sup id="cite_ref-251" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-251">&#91;251&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Scotland_Act_2012" title="Scotland Act 2012">Scotland Act 2012</a>, based on proposals by the commission, was subsequently enacted devolving additional powers to the Scottish Parliament.<sup id="cite_ref-252" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-252">&#91;252&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:FM_meets_with_Juncker.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6b/FM_meets_with_Juncker.jpg/220px-FM_meets_with_Juncker.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="146" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6b/FM_meets_with_Juncker.jpg/330px-FM_meets_with_Juncker.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/6b/FM_meets_with_Juncker.jpg/440px-FM_meets_with_Juncker.jpg 2x" data-file-width="640" data-file-height="425" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:FM_meets_with_Juncker.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>The <a href="/wiki/President_of_the_European_Commission" title="President of the European Commission">president of the European Commission</a>, <a href="/wiki/Jean-Claude_Juncker" title="Jean-Claude Juncker">Jean-Claude Juncker</a> and first minister Nicola Sturgeon</div></div></div>
<p>In August 2009 the SNP proposed a bill to hold a referendum on independence in November 2010. Opposition from all other major parties led to an expected defeat.<sup id="cite_ref-ReferendumBill2010_253-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-ReferendumBill2010-253">&#91;253&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Times3Sep09_254-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Times3Sep09-254">&#91;254&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-255" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-255">&#91;255&#93;</a></sup> After the <a href="/wiki/2011_Scottish_Parliament_election" title="2011 Scottish Parliament election">2011 Scottish Parliament election</a> gave the SNP an overall majority in the Scottish Parliament, the <a href="/wiki/2014_Scottish_independence_referendum" title="2014 Scottish independence referendum">2014 Scottish independence referendum</a> was held on 18 September.<sup id="cite_ref-256" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-256">&#91;256&#93;</a></sup> The referendum resulted in a rejection of independence, by 55.3% to 44.7%.<sup id="cite_ref-257" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-257">&#91;257&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-258" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-258">&#91;258&#93;</a></sup> During the campaign, the three main parties in the British Parliament pledged to extend the powers of the Scottish Parliament.<sup id="cite_ref-259" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-259">&#91;259&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-kelvin_260-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-kelvin-260">&#91;260&#93;</a></sup> An all-party <a href="/wiki/Smith_Commission" title="Smith Commission">commission</a> chaired by <a href="/wiki/Robert_Smith,_Baron_Smith_of_Kelvin" title="Robert Smith, Baron Smith of Kelvin">Robert Smith, Baron Smith of Kelvin</a> was formed,<sup id="cite_ref-kelvin_260-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-kelvin-260">&#91;260&#93;</a></sup> which led to a further devolution of powers through the <a href="/wiki/Scotland_Act_2016" title="Scotland Act 2016">Scotland Act 2016</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-261" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-261">&#91;261&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Following the <a href="/wiki/European_Union_Referendum_Act_2015" title="European Union Referendum Act 2015">European Union Referendum Act 2015</a>, the <a href="/wiki/2016_United_Kingdom_European_Union_membership_referendum" title="2016 United Kingdom European Union membership referendum">2016 United Kingdom European Union membership referendum</a> was held on 23 June 2016 on Britain's membership of the <a href="/wiki/European_Union" title="European Union">European Union</a>. A majority in the United Kingdom voted to withdraw from the EU, whilst a majority within Scotland voted to remain a member.<sup id="cite_ref-:2_262-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:2-262">&#91;262&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The first minister, Nicola Sturgeon, announced the following day that as a result a <a href="/wiki/Proposed_second_Scottish_independence_referendum" title="Proposed second Scottish independence referendum">new independence referendum</a> was "highly likely".<sup id="cite_ref-263" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-263">&#91;263&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:2_262-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:2-262">&#91;262&#93;</a></sup> On 31 January 2020, the United Kingdom formally withdrew from the European Union. At Holyrood, Sturgeon's governing SNP continues to campaign for such a referendum; in December 2019 a formal request for the powers to hold one under Section 30 of the Scotland Act was submitted.<sup id="cite_ref-264" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-264">&#91;264&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-265" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-265">&#91;265&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-266" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-266">&#91;266&#93;</a></sup> In June 2022, Sturgeon announced plans to hold a referendum on 19 October 2023.<sup id="cite_ref-267" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-267">&#91;267&#93;</a></sup> At Westminster, the governing <a href="/wiki/Second_Johnson_ministry" title="Second Johnson ministry">second Johnson ministry</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Conservative_Party_(UK)" title="Conservative Party (UK)">Conservative Party</a> is opposed to another referendum and has refused the first minister's request.<sup id="cite_ref-268" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-268">&#91;268&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:3_269-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:3-269">&#91;269&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-270" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-270">&#91;270&#93;</a></sup> Because constitutional affairs are reserved matters under the Scotland Act, the Scottish Parliament would again have to be granted temporary additional powers under Section 30 in order to hold a legally binding vote.<sup id="cite_ref-:3_269-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:3-269">&#91;269&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-271" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-271">&#91;271&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-272" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-272">&#91;272&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Scotland has <a href="/wiki/Scandinavian_Scotland" title="Scandinavian Scotland">historical and cultural</a> ties with northern countries outside the British Isles, such as the countries of <a href="/wiki/Scandinavia" title="Scandinavia">Scandinavia</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-273" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-273">&#91;273&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-274" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-274">&#91;274&#93;</a></sup> Scottish Government policy advocates for stronger political relations with the <a href="/wiki/Nordic_countries" title="Nordic countries">Nordic</a> and <a href="/wiki/Baltic_states" title="Baltic states">Baltic</a> countries, which has resulted in some Nordic-inspired policies being adopted such as baby boxes.<sup id="cite_ref-:11_275-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:11-275">&#91;275&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-276" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-276">&#91;276&#93;</a></sup> Advocates of Scottish independence argue that, if Scotland were independent, it could become the 'sixth Nordic country'.<sup id="cite_ref-277" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-277">&#91;277&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-278" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-278">&#91;278&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-279" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-279">&#91;279&#93;</a></sup> This idea has received mixed responses from Nordic people.<sup id="cite_ref-280" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-280">&#91;280&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-:11_275-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:11-275">&#91;275&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Administrative_subdivisions">Administrative subdivisions</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Subdivisions_of_Scotland" title="Subdivisions of Scotland">Subdivisions of Scotland</a></div>
<div class="thumb tleft"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Glasgow_City_Chambers_Exterior.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f6/Glasgow_City_Chambers_Exterior.jpg/220px-Glasgow_City_Chambers_Exterior.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f6/Glasgow_City_Chambers_Exterior.jpg/330px-Glasgow_City_Chambers_Exterior.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f6/Glasgow_City_Chambers_Exterior.jpg/440px-Glasgow_City_Chambers_Exterior.jpg 2x" data-file-width="8688" data-file-height="5792" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Glasgow_City_Chambers_Exterior.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div><a href="/wiki/Glasgow_City_Chambers" title="Glasgow City Chambers">Glasgow City Chambers</a>, seat of <a href="/wiki/Glasgow_City_Council" title="Glasgow City Council">Glasgow City Council</a></div></div></div>
<p>Historical subdivisions of Scotland included the <a href="/wiki/Mormaerdom" class="mw-redirect" title="Mormaerdom">mormaerdom</a>, <a href="/wiki/Stewartries" class="mw-redirect" title="Stewartries">stewartry</a>, <a href="/wiki/Earldom" class="mw-redirect" title="Earldom">earldom</a>, <a href="/wiki/Burgh" title="Burgh">burgh</a>, <a href="/wiki/Civil_parishes_in_Scotland" title="Civil parishes in Scotland">parish</a>, <a href="/wiki/Counties_of_Scotland" class="mw-redirect" title="Counties of Scotland">county</a> and <a href="/wiki/Regions_and_districts_of_Scotland" class="mw-redirect" title="Regions and districts of Scotland">regions and districts</a>. Some of these names are still sometimes used as geographical descriptors.<sup id="cite_ref-:9_281-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:9-281">&#91;281&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Modern Scotland is subdivided in various ways depending on the purpose. In local government, there have been 32 single-tier council areas since 1996,<sup id="cite_ref-282" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-282">&#91;282&#93;</a></sup> whose councils are responsible for the provision of all local government services. Decisions are made by councillors who are elected at <a href="/wiki/Elections_in_Scotland" title="Elections in Scotland">local elections</a> every five years. The head of each council is usually the <a href="/wiki/Lord_Provost" class="mw-redirect" title="Lord Provost">Lord Provost</a> alongside the Leader of the council,<sup id="cite_ref-283" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-283">&#91;283&#93;</a></sup> with a Chief Executive being appointed as director of the council area.<sup id="cite_ref-284" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-284">&#91;284&#93;</a></sup> Community Councils are informal organisations that represent specific sub-divisions within each council area.<sup id="cite_ref-:9_281-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:9-281">&#91;281&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In the Scottish Parliament, there are 73 constituencies and eight regions. For the Parliament of the United Kingdom, there are 59 constituencies. Until 2013, the Scottish fire brigades and police forces were based on a system of regions introduced in 1975. For healthcare and postal districts, and a number of other governmental and non-governmental organisations such as the churches, there are other long-standing methods of subdividing Scotland for the purposes of administration.
</p><p><a href="/wiki/City_status_in_the_United_Kingdom" title="City status in the United Kingdom">City status in the United Kingdom</a> is conferred by <a href="/wiki/Letters_patent" title="Letters patent">letters patent</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-285" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-285">&#91;285&#93;</a></sup> There are eight cities in Scotland: <a href="/wiki/Aberdeen" title="Aberdeen">Aberdeen</a>, <a href="/wiki/Dundee" title="Dundee">Dundee</a>, <a href="/wiki/Dunfermline" title="Dunfermline">Dunfermline</a>, <a href="/wiki/Edinburgh" title="Edinburgh">Edinburgh</a>, <a href="/wiki/Glasgow" title="Glasgow">Glasgow</a>, <a href="/wiki/Inverness" title="Inverness">Inverness</a>, <a href="/wiki/Stirling" title="Stirling">Stirling</a> and <a href="/wiki/Perth,_Scotland" title="Perth, Scotland">Perth</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-286" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-286">&#91;286&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Law_and_criminal_justice">Law and criminal justice</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Scots_law" title="Scots law">Scots law</a></div>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:202px;"><a href="/wiki/File:High_Court_of_Justiciary.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/69/High_Court_of_Justiciary.jpg/200px-High_Court_of_Justiciary.jpg" decoding="async" width="200" height="267" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/69/High_Court_of_Justiciary.jpg/300px-High_Court_of_Justiciary.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/6/69/High_Court_of_Justiciary.jpg/400px-High_Court_of_Justiciary.jpg 2x" data-file-width="600" data-file-height="800" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:High_Court_of_Justiciary.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>The <a href="/wiki/High_Court_of_Justiciary" title="High Court of Justiciary">High Court of Justiciary</a> building, Edinburgh, the supreme criminal court in Scotland</div></div></div>
<p>Scots law has a basis derived from <a href="/wiki/Roman_law" title="Roman law">Roman law</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-287" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-287">&#91;287&#93;</a></sup> combining features of both uncodified <a href="/wiki/Civil_law_(legal_system)" title="Civil law (legal system)">civil law</a>, dating back to the <i><a href="/wiki/Corpus_Juris_Civilis" title="Corpus Juris Civilis">Corpus Juris Civilis</a></i>, and <a href="/wiki/Common_law" title="Common law">common law</a> with <a href="/wiki/Legal_institutions_of_Scotland_in_the_High_Middle_Ages" title="Legal institutions of Scotland in the High Middle Ages">medieval sources</a>. The terms of the Treaty of Union with England in 1707 guaranteed the continued existence of a separate legal system in Scotland from that of England and Wales.<sup id="cite_ref-288" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-288">&#91;288&#93;</a></sup> Prior to 1611, there were several regional law systems in Scotland, most notably <a href="/wiki/Udal_law" title="Udal law">Udal law</a> in <a href="/wiki/Orkney" title="Orkney">Orkney</a> and <a href="/wiki/Shetland" title="Shetland">Shetland</a>, based on old Norse law. Various other systems derived from common <a href="/wiki/Celtic_law" title="Celtic law">Celtic</a> or <a href="/wiki/Brehon_laws" class="mw-redirect" title="Brehon laws">Brehon laws</a> survived in the Highlands until the 1800s.<sup id="cite_ref-289" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-289">&#91;289&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Scots law provides for three types of <a href="/wiki/Courts_of_Scotland" title="Courts of Scotland">courts</a> responsible for the administration of justice: civil, criminal and <a href="/wiki/Law_of_Arms" class="mw-redirect" title="Law of Arms">heraldic</a>. The supreme civil court is the <a href="/wiki/Court_of_Session" title="Court of Session">Court of Session</a>, although civil <a href="/wiki/Appeal_(law)" class="mw-redirect" title="Appeal (law)">appeals</a> can be taken to the <a href="/wiki/Supreme_Court_of_the_United_Kingdom" title="Supreme Court of the United Kingdom">Supreme Court of the United Kingdom</a> (or before 1 October 2009, the <a href="/wiki/Judicial_functions_of_the_House_of_Lords" title="Judicial functions of the House of Lords">House of Lords</a>). The <a href="/wiki/High_Court_of_Justiciary" title="High Court of Justiciary">High Court of Justiciary</a> is the supreme criminal court in Scotland. The Court of Session is housed at <a href="/wiki/Parliament_House,_Edinburgh" title="Parliament House, Edinburgh">Parliament House</a>, in Edinburgh, which was the home of the pre-Union <a href="/wiki/Parliament_of_Scotland" title="Parliament of Scotland">Parliament of Scotland</a> with the <a href="/wiki/High_Court_of_Justiciary" title="High Court of Justiciary">High Court of Justiciary</a> and the Supreme Court of Appeal currently located at the <a href="/wiki/Lawnmarket" class="mw-redirect" title="Lawnmarket">Lawnmarket</a>. The <a href="/wiki/Sheriff_court" title="Sheriff court">sheriff court</a> is the main criminal and civil court, hearing most cases. There are 49 sheriff courts throughout the country.<sup id="cite_ref-290" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-290">&#91;290&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/District_Courts_of_Scotland" class="mw-redirect" title="District Courts of Scotland">District courts</a> were introduced in 1975 for minor offences and small claims. These were gradually replaced by <a href="/wiki/Justice_of_the_Peace_Court" class="mw-redirect" title="Justice of the Peace Court">Justice of the Peace Courts</a> from 2008 to 2010. The <a href="/wiki/Court_of_the_Lord_Lyon" title="Court of the Lord Lyon">Court of the Lord Lyon</a> regulates heraldry.
</p><p>For three centuries the Scots legal system was unique for being the only national legal system without a parliament. This ended with the advent of the Scottish Parliament in 1999, which legislates for Scotland. Many features within the system have been preserved. Within criminal law, the Scots legal system is unique in having three possible verdicts: "guilty", "not guilty" and "<i><a href="/wiki/Not_proven" title="Not proven">not proven</a></i>".<sup id="cite_ref-291" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-291">&#91;291&#93;</a></sup> Both "not guilty" and "not proven" result in an <a href="/wiki/Acquittal" title="Acquittal">acquittal</a>, typically with no possibility of retrial in accordance with the rule of <a href="/wiki/Double_jeopardy" title="Double jeopardy">double jeopardy</a>. A retrial can hear new evidence at a later date that might have proven conclusive in the earlier trial at first instance, where the person acquitted subsequently admits the offence or where it can be proved that the acquittal was tainted by an attempt to <a href="/wiki/Perverting_the_course_of_justice" title="Perverting the course of justice">pervert the course of justice</a> – see the provisions of the <a href="/wiki/Double_jeopardy#Scotland" title="Double jeopardy">Double Jeopardy (Scotland) Act 2011</a>. Many laws differ between Scotland and the other parts of the United Kingdom, and many terms differ for certain legal concepts. <a href="/wiki/Manslaughter" title="Manslaughter">Manslaughter</a>, in England and Wales, is broadly similar to <a href="/wiki/Culpable_homicide" title="Culpable homicide">culpable homicide</a> in Scotland, and arson is called <a href="/wiki/Wilful_fire_raising" title="Wilful fire raising">wilful fire raising</a>. Indeed, some acts considered crimes in England and Wales, such as forgery, are not so in Scotland. Procedure also differs. Scots juries, sitting in criminal cases, consist of fifteen jurors, which is three more than is typical in many countries.<sup id="cite_ref-292" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-292">&#91;292&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Scottish_Prison_Service" title="Scottish Prison Service">Scottish Prison Service</a> (SPS) manages the prisons in Scotland, which collectively house over 8,500 prisoners.<sup id="cite_ref-293" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-293">&#91;293&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Cabinet_Secretary_for_Justice" class="mw-redirect" title="Cabinet Secretary for Justice">Cabinet Secretary for Justice</a> is responsible for the Scottish Prison Service within the Scottish Government.
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Health_care">Health care</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Healthcare_in_Scotland" title="Healthcare in Scotland">Healthcare in Scotland</a></div>
<div class="thumb tleft"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:View_along_the_access_road_towards_the_new_Southern_General_Hospital_(geograph_4542089).jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7c/View_along_the_access_road_towards_the_new_Southern_General_Hospital_%28geograph_4542089%29.jpg/220px-View_along_the_access_road_towards_the_new_Southern_General_Hospital_%28geograph_4542089%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="124" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7c/View_along_the_access_road_towards_the_new_Southern_General_Hospital_%28geograph_4542089%29.jpg/330px-View_along_the_access_road_towards_the_new_Southern_General_Hospital_%28geograph_4542089%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/7c/View_along_the_access_road_towards_the_new_Southern_General_Hospital_%28geograph_4542089%29.jpg/440px-View_along_the_access_road_towards_the_new_Southern_General_Hospital_%28geograph_4542089%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="640" data-file-height="360" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:View_along_the_access_road_towards_the_new_Southern_General_Hospital_(geograph_4542089).jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div><a href="/wiki/NHS_Scotland" title="NHS Scotland">NHS Scotland</a>'s <a href="/wiki/Queen_Elizabeth_University_Hospital" title="Queen Elizabeth University Hospital">Queen Elizabeth University Hospital</a>, Glasgow. It is the largest hospital campus in Europe.<sup id="cite_ref-294" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-294">&#91;294&#93;</a></sup></div></div></div>
<p>Health care in Scotland is mainly provided by <a href="/wiki/NHS_Scotland" title="NHS Scotland">NHS Scotland</a>, Scotland's public health care system. This was founded by the <a href="/wiki/National_Health_Service_(Scotland)_Act_1947" title="National Health Service (Scotland) Act 1947">National Health Service (Scotland) Act 1947</a> (later repealed by the National Health Service (Scotland) Act 1978) that took effect on 5 July 1948 to coincide with the launch of the NHS in England and Wales. Prior to 1948, half of Scotland's landmass was already covered by state-funded health care, provided by the <a href="/wiki/Highlands_and_Islands_Medical_Service" title="Highlands and Islands Medical Service">Highlands and Islands Medical Service</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-295" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-295">&#91;295&#93;</a></sup> Healthcare policy and funding is the responsibility of the Scottish Government's <a href="/wiki/Scottish_Government_Health_Directorates" class="mw-redirect" title="Scottish Government Health Directorates">Health Directorates</a>.
</p><p>In 2008, the NHS in Scotland had around 158,000 staff including more than 47,500 nurses, midwives and health visitors and over 3,800 consultants. There are also more than 12,000 doctors, family practitioners and allied health professionals, including dentists, opticians and community pharmacists, who operate as independent contractors providing a range of services within the NHS in return for fees and allowances. These fees and allowances were removed in May 2010, and prescriptions are entirely free, although dentists and opticians may charge if the patient's household earns over a certain amount, about £30,000 per annum.<sup id="cite_ref-296" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-296">&#91;296&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Economy">Economy</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Economy_of_Scotland" title="Economy of Scotland">Economy of Scotland</a></div>
<div class="thumb tleft"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Beryl_alpha_from_air.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/da/Beryl_alpha_from_air.jpg/220px-Beryl_alpha_from_air.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="163" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/da/Beryl_alpha_from_air.jpg/330px-Beryl_alpha_from_air.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/da/Beryl_alpha_from_air.jpg/440px-Beryl_alpha_from_air.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1024" data-file-height="759" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Beryl_alpha_from_air.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>An oil platform in the <a href="/wiki/North_Sea" title="North Sea">North Sea</a></div></div></div>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Skyline_of_Edinburgh.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1a/Skyline_of_Edinburgh.jpg/220px-Skyline_of_Edinburgh.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="124" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1a/Skyline_of_Edinburgh.jpg/330px-Skyline_of_Edinburgh.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1a/Skyline_of_Edinburgh.jpg/440px-Skyline_of_Edinburgh.jpg 2x" data-file-width="5312" data-file-height="2988" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Skyline_of_Edinburgh.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div><a href="/wiki/Edinburgh" title="Edinburgh">Edinburgh</a>, the 13th-largest financial centre in the world and 4th largest in Europe in 2020<sup id="cite_ref-297" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-297">&#91;297&#93;</a></sup></div></div></div>
<p>Scotland has a Western-style <a href="/wiki/Open_economy" title="Open economy">open</a> <a href="/wiki/Mixed_economy" title="Mixed economy">mixed economy</a> closely linked with the rest of the UK and the wider world. Traditionally, the Scottish economy was dominated by <a href="/wiki/Heavy_industry" title="Heavy industry">heavy industry</a> underpinned by shipbuilding in Glasgow, coal mining and <a href="/wiki/Steel_making" class="mw-redirect" title="Steel making">steel industries</a>. Petroleum related industries associated with the extraction of <a href="/wiki/North_Sea_oil" title="North Sea oil">North Sea oil</a> have also been important employers from the 1970s, especially in the north-east of Scotland. De-industrialisation during the 1970s and 1980s saw a shift from a manufacturing focus towards a more <a href="/wiki/Tertiary_sector_of_economic_activity" class="mw-redirect" title="Tertiary sector of economic activity">service</a>-oriented economy.
</p><p>Scotland's gross domestic product (GDP), including oil and gas produced in Scottish waters, was estimated at £150&#160;billion for the calendar year 2012.<sup id="cite_ref-298" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-298">&#91;298&#93;</a></sup> In 2014, Scotland's per capita GDP was one of the highest in the EU.<sup id="cite_ref-299" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-299">&#91;299&#93;</a></sup> As of April 2019 the Scottish unemployment rate was 3.3%, below the UK's overall rate of 3.8%, and the Scottish employment rate was 75.9%.<sup id="cite_ref-300" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-300">&#91;300&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Edinburgh is the financial services centre of Scotland, with many large finance firms based there, including: <a href="/wiki/Lloyds_Banking_Group" title="Lloyds Banking Group">Lloyds Banking Group</a> (owners of <a href="/wiki/HBOS" title="HBOS">HBOS</a>); the Government-owned <a href="/wiki/Royal_Bank_of_Scotland" title="Royal Bank of Scotland">Royal Bank of Scotland</a> and <a href="/wiki/Standard_Life" title="Standard Life">Standard Life</a>. Edinburgh was ranked 15th in the <a href="/wiki/Global_Financial_Centres_Index" title="Global Financial Centres Index">list of world financial centres</a> in 2007, but fell to 37th in 2012, following damage to its reputation,<sup id="cite_ref-301" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-301">&#91;301&#93;</a></sup> and in 2016 was ranked 56th out of 86.<sup id="cite_ref-302" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-302">&#91;302&#93;</a></sup> Its status had returned to 17th by 2020.<sup id="cite_ref-303" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-303">&#91;303&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:NS5864_-_The_River_Clyde_in_Glasgow.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/78/NS5864_-_The_River_Clyde_in_Glasgow.jpg/220px-NS5864_-_The_River_Clyde_in_Glasgow.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/78/NS5864_-_The_River_Clyde_in_Glasgow.jpg/330px-NS5864_-_The_River_Clyde_in_Glasgow.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/7/78/NS5864_-_The_River_Clyde_in_Glasgow.jpg/440px-NS5864_-_The_River_Clyde_in_Glasgow.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1600" data-file-height="1200" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:NS5864_-_The_River_Clyde_in_Glasgow.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>The <a href="/wiki/International_Financial_Services_District" title="International Financial Services District">International Financial Services District</a> in Glasgow, a major financial district in Scotland</div></div></div>
<p>In 2014, total Scottish exports (excluding intra-UK trade) were estimated to be £27.5&#160;billion.<sup id="cite_ref-304" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-304">&#91;304&#93;</a></sup> Scotland's primary exports include <a href="/wiki/Whisky" title="Whisky">whisky</a>, electronics and financial services.<sup id="cite_ref-Trade_305-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Trade-305">&#91;305&#93;</a></sup> The United States, Netherlands, Germany, France, and Norway constitute the country's major export markets.<sup id="cite_ref-Trade_305-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Trade-305">&#91;305&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Whisky is one of Scotland's more known goods of economic activity. Exports increased by 87% in the decade to 2012<sup id="cite_ref-306" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-306">&#91;306&#93;</a></sup> and were valued at £4.3&#160;billion in 2013, which was 85% of Scotland's food and drink exports.<sup id="cite_ref-307" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-307">&#91;307&#93;</a></sup> It supports around 10,000 jobs directly and 25,000 indirectly.<sup id="cite_ref-308" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-308">&#91;308&#93;</a></sup> It may contribute £400–682&#160;million to Scotland, rather than several billion pounds, as more than 80% of whisky produced is owned by non-Scottish companies.<sup id="cite_ref-309" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-309">&#91;309&#93;</a></sup> A briefing published in 2002 by the Scottish Parliament Information Centre (SPICe) for the Scottish Parliament's Enterprise and Life Long Learning Committee stated that tourism accounted for up to 5% of GDP and 7.5% of employment.<sup id="cite_ref-310" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-310">&#91;310&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Scotland was one of the industrial powerhouses of Europe from the time of the <a href="/wiki/Industrial_Revolution" title="Industrial Revolution">Industrial Revolution</a> onwards, being a world leader in manufacturing.<sup id="cite_ref-311" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-311">&#91;311&#93;</a></sup> This left a legacy in the diversity of goods and services which Scotland produces, from textiles, <a href="/wiki/Whisky" title="Whisky">whisky</a> and <a href="/wiki/Shortbread" title="Shortbread">shortbread</a> to jet engines, buses, computer software, ships, <a href="/wiki/Avionics" title="Avionics">avionics</a> and <a href="/wiki/Microelectronics" title="Microelectronics">microelectronics</a>, as well as banking, insurance, <a href="/wiki/Investment_management" title="Investment management">investment management</a> and other related financial services.<sup id="cite_ref-312" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-312">&#91;312&#93;</a></sup> In common with most other advanced industrialised economies, Scotland has seen a decline in the importance of both manufacturing industries and primary-based extractive industries. This has been combined with a rise in the <a href="/wiki/Tertiary_sector_of_the_economy" title="Tertiary sector of the economy">service</a> sector of the economy, which has grown to be the largest sector in Scotland.<sup id="cite_ref-313" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-313">&#91;313&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Museum_on_the_mound,_Edinburgh_(28252011008).jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/47/Museum_on_the_mound%2C_Edinburgh_%2828252011008%29.jpg/220px-Museum_on_the_mound%2C_Edinburgh_%2828252011008%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="131" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/47/Museum_on_the_mound%2C_Edinburgh_%2828252011008%29.jpg/330px-Museum_on_the_mound%2C_Edinburgh_%2828252011008%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/47/Museum_on_the_mound%2C_Edinburgh_%2828252011008%29.jpg/440px-Museum_on_the_mound%2C_Edinburgh_%2828252011008%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="6000" data-file-height="3580" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Museum_on_the_mound,_Edinburgh_(28252011008).jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>The <a href="/wiki/Bank_of_Scotland" title="Bank of Scotland">Bank of Scotland</a> has its headquarters in Edinburgh and is one of the oldest operating banks in the world.</div></div></div>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Currency">Currency</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Banknotes_of_Scotland" title="Banknotes of Scotland">Banknotes of Scotland</a></div>
<p>Although the <a href="/wiki/Bank_of_England" title="Bank of England">Bank of England</a> is the <a href="/wiki/Central_bank" title="Central bank">central bank</a> for the UK, three Scottish <a href="/wiki/Clearing_bank_(United_Kingdom)" class="mw-redirect" title="Clearing bank (United Kingdom)">clearing banks</a> issue <a href="/wiki/Pound_sterling" title="Pound sterling">Sterling</a> <a href="/wiki/Banknote" title="Banknote">banknotes</a>: the <a href="/wiki/Bank_of_Scotland" title="Bank of Scotland">Bank of Scotland</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Royal_Bank_of_Scotland" title="Royal Bank of Scotland">Royal Bank of Scotland</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Clydesdale_Bank" title="Clydesdale Bank">Clydesdale Bank</a>. The issuing of banknotes by <a href="/wiki/Retail_bank" class="mw-redirect" title="Retail bank">retail banks</a> in Scotland is subject to the <a href="/wiki/Banking_Act_2009" title="Banking Act 2009">Banking Act 2009</a>, which repealed all earlier legislation under which banknote issuance was regulated, and the Scottish and Northern Ireland Banknote Regulations 2009.<sup id="cite_ref-314" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-314">&#91;314&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The value of the Scottish banknotes in circulation in 2013 was £3.8&#160;billion, underwritten by the Bank of England using funds deposited by each clearing bank, under the <a href="/wiki/Banking_Act_2009" title="Banking Act 2009">Banking Act 2009</a>, in order to cover the total value of such notes in circulation.<sup id="cite_ref-Banknotes_315-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Banknotes-315">&#91;315&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<div style="clear:both;"></div>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Military">Military</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/British_Armed_Forces" title="British Armed Forces">British Armed Forces</a> and <a href="/wiki/Military_history_of_Scotland" title="Military history of Scotland">Military history of Scotland</a></div>
<div class="thumb tleft"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Challenger2-Bergen-Hohne-Training-Area-2.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/18/Challenger2-Bergen-Hohne-Training-Area-2.jpg/220px-Challenger2-Bergen-Hohne-Training-Area-2.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="119" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/18/Challenger2-Bergen-Hohne-Training-Area-2.jpg/330px-Challenger2-Bergen-Hohne-Training-Area-2.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/18/Challenger2-Bergen-Hohne-Training-Area-2.jpg/440px-Challenger2-Bergen-Hohne-Training-Area-2.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2580" data-file-height="1400" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Challenger2-Bergen-Hohne-Training-Area-2.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>A <a href="/wiki/Challenger_2" title="Challenger 2">Challenger 2</a> <a href="/wiki/Main_battle_tank" title="Main battle tank">main battle tank</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Royal_Scots_Dragoon_Guards" title="Royal Scots Dragoon Guards">Royal Scots Dragoon Guards</a></div></div></div>
<p>Of the money spent on UK defence, about £3.3&#160;billion can be attributed to Scotland as of 2018/2019.<sup id="cite_ref-316" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-316">&#91;316&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Scotland had a long military tradition predating the <a href="/wiki/Treaty_of_Union" title="Treaty of Union">Treaty of Union</a> with England; the <a href="/wiki/Scots_Army" title="Scots Army">Scots Army</a> and <a href="/wiki/Royal_Scots_Navy" title="Royal Scots Navy">Royal Scots Navy</a> were (with the exception of the <a href="/wiki/Atholl_Highlanders" title="Atholl Highlanders">Atholl Highlanders</a>, Europe's only legal <a href="/wiki/Private_army" title="Private army">private army</a>) merged with their English counterparts to form the <a href="/wiki/Royal_Navy" title="Royal Navy">Royal Navy</a> and the <a href="/wiki/British_Army" title="British Army">British Army</a>, which together form part of the <a href="/wiki/British_Armed_Forces" title="British Armed Forces">British Armed Forces</a>. Numerous <a href="/wiki/Scottish_regiment" title="Scottish regiment">Scottish regiments</a> have at various times existed in the British Army. Distinctively Scottish regiments in the British Army include the <a href="/wiki/Scots_Guards" title="Scots Guards">Scots Guards</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Royal_Scots_Dragoon_Guards" title="Royal Scots Dragoon Guards">Royal Scots Dragoon Guards</a> and the <a href="/wiki/154_(Scottish)_Regiment_RLC" title="154 (Scottish) Regiment RLC">154 (Scottish) Regiment RLC</a>, an <a href="/wiki/Army_Reserve_(United_Kingdom)" title="Army Reserve (United Kingdom)">Army Reserve</a> regiment of the <a href="/wiki/Royal_Logistic_Corps" title="Royal Logistic Corps">Royal Logistic Corps</a>. In 2006, as a result of the <i><a href="/wiki/Delivering_Security_in_a_Changing_World" title="Delivering Security in a Changing World">Delivering Security in a Changing World</a></i> <a href="/wiki/White_paper" title="White paper">white paper</a>, the Scottish infantry regiments in the <a href="/wiki/Scottish_Division" title="Scottish Division">Scottish Division</a> were amalgamated to form the <a href="/wiki/Royal_Regiment_of_Scotland" title="Royal Regiment of Scotland">Royal Regiment of Scotland</a>. As a result of the <a href="/wiki/Cameron%E2%80%93Clegg_coalition" title="Cameron–Clegg coalition">Cameron–Clegg coalition</a>'s <a href="/wiki/Strategic_Defence_and_Security_Review_2010" title="Strategic Defence and Security Review 2010">Strategic Defence and Security Review 2010</a>, the Scottish regiments of the line in the <a href="/wiki/British_Army" title="British Army">British Army</a> <a href="/wiki/Infantry_of_the_British_Army" title="Infantry of the British Army">infantry</a>, having previously formed the Scottish Division, were reorganised into the <a href="/wiki/Scottish,_Welsh_and_Irish_Division" title="Scottish, Welsh and Irish Division">Scottish, Welsh and Irish Division</a> in 2017. Before the formation of the Scottish Division, the Scottish infantry was organised into a <a href="/wiki/Lowland_Brigade_(United_Kingdom)" title="Lowland Brigade (United Kingdom)">Lowland Brigade</a> and <a href="/wiki/Highland_Brigade_(United_Kingdom)" title="Highland Brigade (United Kingdom)">Highland Brigade</a>.
</p>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Eurofighter_Typhoon,_ZK312_(19451923880).jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/99/Eurofighter_Typhoon%2C_ZK312_%2819451923880%29.jpg/220px-Eurofighter_Typhoon%2C_ZK312_%2819451923880%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/99/Eurofighter_Typhoon%2C_ZK312_%2819451923880%29.jpg/330px-Eurofighter_Typhoon%2C_ZK312_%2819451923880%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/99/Eurofighter_Typhoon%2C_ZK312_%2819451923880%29.jpg/440px-Eurofighter_Typhoon%2C_ZK312_%2819451923880%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1024" data-file-height="682" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Eurofighter_Typhoon,_ZK312_(19451923880).jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>A <a href="/wiki/Eurofighter_Typhoon" title="Eurofighter Typhoon">Typhoon FGR4</a> in <a href="/wiki/No._6_Squadron_RAF" title="No. 6 Squadron RAF">No. 6 Squadron</a> markings taking off from runway 23 at Lossiemouth</div></div></div>
<p>Because of their topography and perceived remoteness, parts of Scotland have housed many sensitive defence establishments.<sup id="cite_ref-317" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-317">&#91;317&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-318" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-318">&#91;318&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-319" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-319">&#91;319&#93;</a></sup> Between 1960 and 1991, the <a href="/wiki/Holy_Loch" title="Holy Loch">Holy Loch</a> was a base for the US fleet of <a href="/wiki/Polaris_ballistic_missile" class="mw-redirect" title="Polaris ballistic missile">Polaris</a> <a href="/wiki/Ballistic_missile_submarine" title="Ballistic missile submarine">ballistic missile submarines</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-320" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-320">&#91;320&#93;</a></sup> Today, <a href="/wiki/Her_Majesty%27s_Naval_Base_Clyde" class="mw-redirect" title="Her Majesty&#39;s Naval Base Clyde">Her Majesty's Naval Base Clyde</a>, 25 miles (40 kilometres) north-west of Glasgow, is the base for the four <a href="/wiki/Trident_(missile)" title="Trident (missile)">Trident</a>-armed <a href="/wiki/Vanguard-class_submarine" title="Vanguard-class submarine"><i> Vanguard</i>-class</a> <a href="/wiki/Ballistic_missile_submarine" title="Ballistic missile submarine">ballistic missile submarines</a> that comprise the Britain's <a href="/wiki/Nuclear_deterrent" class="mw-redirect" title="Nuclear deterrent">nuclear deterrent</a>. <a href="/wiki/Scapa_Flow" title="Scapa Flow">Scapa Flow</a> was the major <a href="/wiki/Grand_Fleet" title="Grand Fleet">Fleet</a> base for the <a href="/wiki/Royal_Navy" title="Royal Navy">Royal Navy</a> until 1956.
</p><p>Scotland's <a href="/wiki/Scapa_Flow" title="Scapa Flow">Scapa Flow</a> was the main base for the <a href="/wiki/Royal_Navy" title="Royal Navy">Royal Navy</a> in the 20th century.<sup id="cite_ref-321" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-321">&#91;321&#93;</a></sup> As the <a href="/wiki/Cold_War" title="Cold War">Cold War</a> intensified in 1961, the United States deployed <a href="/wiki/Polaris_ballistic_missile" class="mw-redirect" title="Polaris ballistic missile">Polaris ballistic missiles</a>, and submarines, in the <a href="/wiki/Firth_of_Clyde" title="Firth of Clyde">Firth of Clyde</a>'s <a href="/wiki/Holy_Loch" title="Holy Loch">Holy Loch</a>. Public protests from <a href="/wiki/CND" class="mw-redirect" title="CND">CND</a> campaigners proved futile. The Royal Navy successfully convinced the government to allow the base because it wanted its own Polaris submarines, and it obtained them in 1963. The RN's nuclear submarine base opened with four <a href="/wiki/Resolution-class_submarine" title="Resolution-class submarine"><i> Resolution</i>-class</a> Polaris submarines at the expanded <a href="/wiki/HMNB_Clyde" title="HMNB Clyde">Faslane Naval Base</a> on the <a href="/wiki/Gare_Loch" title="Gare Loch">Gare Loch</a>. The first patrol of a <a href="/wiki/Trident_missile" class="mw-redirect" title="Trident missile">Trident</a>-armed submarine occurred in 1994, although the US base was closed at the end of the Cold War.<sup id="cite_ref-322" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-322">&#91;322&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>A single front-line <a href="/wiki/Royal_Air_Force" title="Royal Air Force">Royal Air Force</a> base is located in Scotland. <a href="/wiki/RAF_Lossiemouth" title="RAF Lossiemouth">RAF Lossiemouth</a>, located in <a href="/wiki/Moray" title="Moray">Moray</a>, is the most northerly <a href="/wiki/Anti-aircraft_warfare" title="Anti-aircraft warfare">air defence</a> <a href="/wiki/Fighter_aircraft" title="Fighter aircraft">fighter</a> base in the United Kingdom and is home to three fast-jet squadrons equipped with the <a href="/wiki/Eurofighter_Typhoon" title="Eurofighter Typhoon">Eurofighter Typhoon</a>.
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Education">Education</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main articles: <a href="/wiki/Education_in_Scotland" title="Education in Scotland">Education in Scotland</a> and <a href="/wiki/List_of_universities_in_Scotland" title="List of universities in Scotland">List of universities in Scotland</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1096954695/mw-parser-output/.tmulti"/><div class="thumb tmulti tright"><div class="thumbinner multiimageinner" style="width:204px;max-width:204px"><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:202px;max-width:202px"><div class="thumbimage"><a href="/wiki/File:UWS,_Ayr_Campus.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/UWS%2C_Ayr_Campus.jpg/200px-UWS%2C_Ayr_Campus.jpg" decoding="async" width="200" height="160" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/UWS%2C_Ayr_Campus.jpg/300px-UWS%2C_Ayr_Campus.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/43/UWS%2C_Ayr_Campus.jpg/400px-UWS%2C_Ayr_Campus.jpg 2x" data-file-width="693" data-file-height="555" /></a></div><div class="thumbcaption text-align-center">Granted university status in 1992, the <a href="/wiki/University_of_the_West_of_Scotland" title="University of the West of Scotland">University of the West of Scotland</a> (UWS) can trace its history back to 1897, as Paisley College of Technology.</div></div></div><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:202px;max-width:202px"><div class="thumbimage"><a href="/wiki/File:St_Andrews_University_-_geograph.org.uk_-_135908.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4a/St_Andrews_University_-_geograph.org.uk_-_135908.jpg/200px-St_Andrews_University_-_geograph.org.uk_-_135908.jpg" decoding="async" width="200" height="150" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4a/St_Andrews_University_-_geograph.org.uk_-_135908.jpg/300px-St_Andrews_University_-_geograph.org.uk_-_135908.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4a/St_Andrews_University_-_geograph.org.uk_-_135908.jpg/400px-St_Andrews_University_-_geograph.org.uk_-_135908.jpg 2x" data-file-width="600" data-file-height="450" /></a></div><div class="thumbcaption text-align-center"><a href="/wiki/University_of_St_Andrews" title="University of St Andrews">University of St Andrews</a> is the oldest University in Scotland and third oldest in the English-speaking world.</div></div></div></div></div>
<p>The <a href="/wiki/Education_in_Scotland" title="Education in Scotland">Scottish education system</a> has always been distinct from the rest of the United Kingdom, with a characteristic emphasis on a <a href="/wiki/Liberal_education" title="Liberal education">broad education</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-323" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-323">&#91;323&#93;</a></sup> In the 15th century, the Humanist emphasis on education cumulated with the passing of the <a href="/wiki/Education_Act_1496" title="Education Act 1496">Education Act 1496</a>, which decreed that all sons of barons and freeholders of substance should attend grammar schools to learn "perfyct Latyne", resulting in an increase in literacy among a male and wealthy elite.<sup id="cite_ref-Bawcutt&amp;Williams2006pp29-30_324-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Bawcutt&amp;Williams2006pp29-30-324">&#91;324&#93;</a></sup> In the Reformation, the 1560 <i><a href="/wiki/First_Book_of_Discipline" class="mw-redirect" title="First Book of Discipline">First Book of Discipline</a></i> set out a plan for a school in every parish, but this proved financially impossible.<sup id="cite_ref-325" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-325">&#91;325&#93;</a></sup> In 1616 an <a href="/wiki/School_Establishment_Act_1616" title="School Establishment Act 1616">act in Privy council</a> commanded every parish to establish a school.<sup id="cite_ref-326" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-326">&#91;326&#93;</a></sup> By the late seventeenth century there was a largely complete network of parish schools in the lowlands, but in the Highlands basic education was still lacking in many areas.<sup id="cite_ref-Anderson2003_327-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Anderson2003-327">&#91;327&#93;</a></sup> Education remained a matter for the church rather than the state until the <a href="/wiki/Education_(Scotland)_Act_1872" title="Education (Scotland) Act 1872">Education (Scotland) Act 1872</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-328" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-328">&#91;328&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The <i><a href="/wiki/Curriculum_for_Excellence" title="Curriculum for Excellence">Curriculum for Excellence</a></i>, Scotland's national school curriculum, presently provides the curricular framework for children and young people from age 3 to 18.<sup id="cite_ref-329" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-329">&#91;329&#93;</a></sup> All 3- and 4-year-old children in Scotland are entitled to a free nursery place. Formal primary education begins at approximately 5 years old and lasts for 7 years (P1–P7); children in Scotland study National Qualifications of the <a href="/wiki/Curriculum_for_Excellence" title="Curriculum for Excellence">Curriculum for Excellence</a> between the ages of 14 and 18. The school leaving age is 16, after which students may choose to remain at school and study further qualifications. A small number of students at certain private, <a href="/wiki/Independent_school_(UK)" class="mw-redirect" title="Independent school (UK)">independent schools</a> may follow the <a href="/wiki/Education_in_England" title="Education in England">English system</a> and study towards <a href="/wiki/GCSE" class="mw-redirect" title="GCSE">GCSEs</a> and <a href="/wiki/Advanced_Level_(UK)" class="mw-redirect" title="Advanced Level (UK)">A</a> and <a href="/wiki/Advanced_Level_(UK)" class="mw-redirect" title="Advanced Level (UK)">AS-Levels</a> instead.<sup id="cite_ref-330" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-330">&#91;330&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>There are fifteen <a href="/wiki/Scottish_universities" class="mw-redirect" title="Scottish universities">Scottish universities</a>, some of which are amongst the <a href="/wiki/List_of_oldest_universities_in_continuous_operation" title="List of oldest universities in continuous operation">oldest in the world</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-331" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-331">&#91;331&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-332" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-332">&#91;332&#93;</a></sup> The four universities founded before the end of the 16th century – the <a href="/wiki/University_of_St_Andrews" title="University of St Andrews">University of St Andrews</a>, the <a href="/wiki/University_of_Glasgow" title="University of Glasgow">University of Glasgow</a>, the <a href="/wiki/University_of_Aberdeen" title="University of Aberdeen">University of Aberdeen</a> and the <a href="/wiki/University_of_Edinburgh" title="University of Edinburgh">University of Edinburgh</a> – are collectively known as the <a href="/wiki/Ancient_universities_of_Scotland" title="Ancient universities of Scotland">ancient universities of Scotland</a>, all of which rank among the 200 best universities in the world in the <a href="/wiki/Times_Higher_Education_World_University_Rankings" title="Times Higher Education World University Rankings">THE rankings</a>, with Edinburgh placing in the top 50.<sup id="cite_ref-333" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-333">&#91;333&#93;</a></sup> Scotland had more universities per capita in <a href="/wiki/QS_World_University_Rankings" title="QS World University Rankings">QS' World University Rankings'</a> top 100 in 2012 than any other nation.<sup id="cite_ref-334" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-334">&#91;334&#93;</a></sup> The country produces 1% of the world's <a href="/wiki/Academic_publishing" title="Academic publishing">published research</a> with less than 0.1% of the world's population, and higher education institutions account for 9% of Scotland's service sector exports.<sup id="cite_ref-335" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-335">&#91;335&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-336" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-336">&#91;336&#93;</a></sup> Scotland's University Courts are the only bodies in Scotland authorised to award degrees.
</p><p>Tuition fees are handled by the Student Awards Agency Scotland (SAAS), which pays the fees of what it defines as "Young Students". Young Students are defined as those under 25, without children, marriage, civil partnership or cohabiting partner, who have not been outside of full-time education for more than three years. Fees must be paid by those outside the young student definition, typically from £1,200 to £1,800 for undergraduate courses, dependent on year of application and type of qualification. Postgraduate fees can be up to £3,400.<sup id="cite_ref-337" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-337">&#91;337&#93;</a></sup> The system has been in place since 2007 when graduate endowments were abolished.<sup id="cite_ref-www.scotland.gov.uk/News/Releases/2008/02/28172530_338-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-www.scotland.gov.uk/News/Releases/2008/02/28172530-338">&#91;338&#93;</a></sup> Labour's education spokesperson <a href="/wiki/Rhona_Brankin" title="Rhona Brankin">Rhona Brankin</a> criticised the Scottish system for failing to address student poverty.<sup id="cite_ref-339" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-339">&#91;339&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Scotland's universities are complemented in the provision of Further and Higher Education by 43 colleges. Colleges offer National Certificates, Higher National Certificates, and Higher National Diplomas. These Group Awards, alongside Scottish Vocational Qualifications, aim to ensure Scotland's population has the appropriate skills and knowledge to meet workplace needs. In 2014, research reported by the <a href="/wiki/Office_for_National_Statistics" title="Office for National Statistics">Office for National Statistics</a> found that Scotland was the most highly educated country in Europe and among the most well-educated in the world in terms of tertiary education attainment, with roughly 40% of people in Scotland aged 16–64 educated to <a href="/wiki/National_Vocational_Qualification#Levels" title="National Vocational Qualification">NVQ level 4</a> and above.<sup id="cite_ref-340" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-340">&#91;340&#93;</a></sup> Based on the original data for <a href="/wiki/Nomenclature_of_Territorial_Units_for_Statistics" title="Nomenclature of Territorial Units for Statistics">EU statistical regions</a>, all four Scottish regions ranked significantly above the European average for completion of tertiary-level education by 25- to 64-year-olds.<sup id="cite_ref-Eurostat_341-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Eurostat-341">&#91;341&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p><a href="/wiki/Kilmarnock_Academy" title="Kilmarnock Academy">Kilmarnock Academy</a> in <a href="/wiki/East_Ayrshire" title="East Ayrshire">East Ayrshire</a> is one of only two schools in the UK, and the only school in Scotland, to have educated two <a href="/wiki/Nobel_Prize" title="Nobel Prize">Nobel Prize</a> Laureates – <a href="/wiki/Alexander_Fleming" title="Alexander Fleming">Alexander Fleming</a>, discoverer of <a href="/wiki/Penicillin" title="Penicillin">Penicillin</a>, and <a href="/wiki/John_Boyd_Orr,_1st_Baron_Boyd-Orr" class="mw-redirect" title="John Boyd Orr, 1st Baron Boyd-Orr">John Boyd Orr, 1st Baron Boyd-Orr</a>, for his scientific research into <a href="/wiki/Nutrition" title="Nutrition">nutrition</a> and his work as the first Director-General of the <a href="/wiki/United_Nations" title="United Nations">United Nations</a> <a href="/wiki/Food_and_Agriculture_Organization" title="Food and Agriculture Organization">Food and Agriculture Organization</a> (FAO).
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Culture">Culture</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Culture_of_Scotland" title="Culture of Scotland">Culture of Scotland</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Scottish_art" title="Scottish art">Scottish art</a> and <a href="/wiki/Media_of_Scotland" title="Media of Scotland">Media of Scotland</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1096954695/mw-parser-output/.tmulti"/><div class="thumb tmulti tright"><div class="thumbinner multiimageinner" style="width:347px;max-width:347px"><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:183px;max-width:183px"><div class="thumbimage"><a href="/wiki/File:PG_1063Burns_Naysmithcrop.jpg" class="image"><img alt="Half-length portrait of Robert Burns by Alexander Nasmyth" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fb/PG_1063Burns_Naysmithcrop.jpg/181px-PG_1063Burns_Naysmithcrop.jpg" decoding="async" width="181" height="233" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/fb/PG_1063Burns_Naysmithcrop.jpg/272px-PG_1063Burns_Naysmithcrop.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/fb/PG_1063Burns_Naysmithcrop.jpg 2x" data-file-width="295" data-file-height="380" /></a></div></div><div class="tsingle" style="width:160px;max-width:160px"><div class="thumbimage"><a href="/wiki/File:Scottish_piper.jpg" class="image"><img alt="Man playing bagpipes in the Highlands" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f6/Scottish_piper.jpg/158px-Scottish_piper.jpg" decoding="async" width="158" height="236" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f6/Scottish_piper.jpg/237px-Scottish_piper.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/f/f6/Scottish_piper.jpg/316px-Scottish_piper.jpg 2x" data-file-width="800" data-file-height="1195" /></a></div></div></div><div class="trow" style="display:flex"><div class="thumbcaption"><a href="/wiki/Robert_Burns" title="Robert Burns">Robert Burns</a>, regarded as the national poet of Scotland is a well known and respected poet worldwide (left). The <a href="/wiki/Bagpipes" title="Bagpipes">bagpipes</a> are a well known symbol of Scotland and an early example of popular Scottish music (right).</div></div></div></div>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Scottish_music">Scottish music</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Music_of_Scotland" title="Music of Scotland">Music of Scotland</a></div>
