<p><a href="/wiki/Scottish_music" class="mw-redirect" title="Scottish music">Scottish music</a> is a significant aspect of the nation's culture, with both traditional and modern influences. A famous traditional Scottish instrument is the <a href="/wiki/Great_Highland_bagpipe" title="Great Highland bagpipe">Great Highland bagpipe</a>, a wind instrument consisting of three drones and a melody pipe (called the chanter), which are fed continuously by a reservoir of air in a bag. <a href="/wiki/Pipe_band" title="Pipe band">Bagpipe bands</a>, featuring bagpipes and various types of drums, and showcasing Scottish music styles while creating new ones, have spread throughout the world. The <a href="/wiki/Cl%C3%A0rsach" class="mw-redirect" title="Clàrsach">clàrsach</a> (harp), <a href="/wiki/Musical_styles_(violin)#Fiddle" class="mw-redirect" title="Musical styles (violin)">fiddle</a> and <a href="/wiki/Accordion" title="Accordion">accordion</a> are also traditional Scottish instruments, the latter two heavily featured in <a href="/wiki/Scottish_country_dance" title="Scottish country dance">Scottish country dance</a> bands. There are many successful Scottish bands and individual artists in varying styles including <a href="/wiki/Annie_Lennox" title="Annie Lennox">Annie Lennox</a>, <a href="/wiki/Amy_Macdonald" title="Amy Macdonald">Amy Macdonald</a>, <a href="/wiki/Runrig" title="Runrig">Runrig</a>, <a href="/wiki/Belle_and_Sebastian" title="Belle and Sebastian">Belle and Sebastian</a>, <a href="/wiki/Boards_of_Canada" title="Boards of Canada">Boards of Canada</a>, <a href="/wiki/Camera_Obscura_(band)" title="Camera Obscura (band)">Camera Obscura</a>, <a href="/wiki/Cocteau_Twins" title="Cocteau Twins">Cocteau Twins</a>, <a href="/wiki/Deacon_Blue" title="Deacon Blue">Deacon Blue</a>, <a href="/wiki/Franz_Ferdinand_(band)" title="Franz Ferdinand (band)">Franz Ferdinand</a>, <a href="/wiki/Susan_Boyle" title="Susan Boyle">Susan Boyle</a>, <a href="/wiki/Emeli_Sand%C3%A9" title="Emeli Sandé">Emeli Sandé</a>, <a href="/wiki/Texas_(band)" title="Texas (band)">Texas</a>, <a href="/wiki/The_View_(band)" title="The View (band)">The View</a>, <a href="/wiki/The_Fratellis" title="The Fratellis">The Fratellis</a>, <a href="/wiki/Twin_Atlantic" title="Twin Atlantic">Twin Atlantic</a>, <a href="/wiki/Bay_City_Rollers" title="Bay City Rollers">Bay City Rollers</a> and <a href="/wiki/Biffy_Clyro" title="Biffy Clyro">Biffy Clyro</a>. Other Scottish musicians include <a href="/wiki/Shirley_Manson" title="Shirley Manson">Shirley Manson</a>, <a href="/wiki/Paolo_Nutini" title="Paolo Nutini">Paolo Nutini</a>, <a href="/wiki/Andy_Stewart_(musician)" title="Andy Stewart (musician)">Andy Stewart</a> and <a href="/wiki/Calvin_Harris" title="Calvin Harris">Calvin Harris</a>, all of whom have achieved considerable commercial success in international music markets<sup id="cite_ref-342" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-342">&#91;342&#93;</a></sup> Shirley Manson performed at the 1999 opening of the <a href="/wiki/Scottish_Parliament" title="Scottish Parliament">Scottish Parliament</a> concert at <a href="/wiki/Princes_Street_Gardens" title="Princes Street Gardens">Princes Street Gardens</a> with her band <a href="/wiki/Garbage_(band)" title="Garbage (band)">Garbage</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-343" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-343">&#91;343&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Rock band <a href="/wiki/Simple_Minds" title="Simple Minds">Simple Minds</a> were the most commercially successful Scottish band of the 1980s, having found success in international markets such as the United States, Canada, Australia and New Zealand,<sup id="cite_ref-344" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-344">&#91;344&#93;</a></sup> whilst pop singer <a href="/wiki/Lewis_Capaldi" title="Lewis Capaldi">Lewis Capaldi</a> was recognised as the best selling artist in the UK in 2019.<sup id="cite_ref-345" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-345">&#91;345&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Awards in recognition of Scottish musical talent in Scotland include the <a href="/wiki/Scottish_Music_Awards" title="Scottish Music Awards">Scottish Music Awards</a>, <a href="/wiki/Scottish_Album_of_the_Year_Award" title="Scottish Album of the Year Award">Scottish Album of the Year Award</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Scots_Trad_Music_Awards" title="Scots Trad Music Awards">Scots Trad Music Awards</a> and the <a href="/wiki/BBC_Radio_Scotland_Young_Traditional_Musician" title="BBC Radio Scotland Young Traditional Musician">BBC Radio Scotland Young Traditional Musician</a> award.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Literature">Literature</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Scottish_literature" title="Scottish literature">Scottish literature</a></div>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1096954695/mw-parser-output/.tmulti"/><div class="thumb tmulti tright"><div class="thumbinner multiimageinner" style="width:342px;max-width:342px"><div class="trow"><div class="theader">Scottish authors and novelists</div></div><div class="trow"><div class="tsingle" style="width:97px;max-width:97px"><div class="thumbimage" style="height:151px;overflow:hidden"><a href="/wiki/File:Conan_doyle.jpg" class="image"><img alt="Conan Doyle" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bb/Conan_doyle.jpg/95px-Conan_doyle.jpg" decoding="async" width="95" height="152" data-file-width="1403" data-file-height="2238" /></a></div><div class="thumbcaption">Sir <a href="/wiki/Arthur_Conan_Doyle" title="Arthur Conan Doyle">Arthur Conan Doyle</a>, creator of <a href="/wiki/Sherlock_Holmes" title="Sherlock Holmes">Sherlock Holmes</a></div></div><div class="tsingle" style="width:116px;max-width:116px"><div class="thumbimage" style="height:151px;overflow:hidden"><a href="/wiki/File:IanRankin_ExitMusic.jpg" class="image"><img alt="Ian Rankin" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/21/IanRankin_ExitMusic.jpg/114px-IanRankin_ExitMusic.jpg" decoding="async" width="114" height="152" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/21/IanRankin_ExitMusic.jpg/171px-IanRankin_ExitMusic.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/2/21/IanRankin_ExitMusic.jpg/228px-IanRankin_ExitMusic.jpg 2x" data-file-width="734" data-file-height="979" /></a></div><div class="thumbcaption">Sir <a href="/wiki/Ian_Rankin" title="Ian Rankin">Ian Rankin</a>, writer of the <a href="/wiki/Inspector_Rebus" title="Inspector Rebus">Inspector Rebus</a> novels</div></div><div class="tsingle" style="width:123px;max-width:123px"><div class="thumbimage" style="height:151px;overflow:hidden"><a href="/wiki/File:Robert_Louis_Stevenson_1885.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/Robert_Louis_Stevenson_1885.jpg/121px-Robert_Louis_Stevenson_1885.jpg" decoding="async" width="121" height="152" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/Robert_Louis_Stevenson_1885.jpg/182px-Robert_Louis_Stevenson_1885.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/Robert_Louis_Stevenson_1885.jpg/242px-Robert_Louis_Stevenson_1885.jpg 2x" data-file-width="817" data-file-height="1024" /></a></div><div class="thumbcaption"><a href="/wiki/Robert_Louis_Stevenson" title="Robert Louis Stevenson">Robert Louis Stevenson</a>, writer of <a href="/wiki/Treasure_Island" title="Treasure Island">Treasure Island</a></div></div></div></div></div>
<p>Scotland has a literary heritage dating back to the early Middle Ages. The earliest extant literature composed in what is now Scotland was in <a href="/wiki/Brythonic_languages" class="mw-redirect" title="Brythonic languages">Brythonic</a> speech in the 6th century, but is preserved as part of <a href="/wiki/Welsh-language_literature" title="Welsh-language literature">Welsh literature</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-346" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-346">&#91;346&#93;</a></sup> Later medieval literature included works in Latin,<sup id="cite_ref-347" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-347">&#91;347&#93;</a></sup> Gaelic,<sup id="cite_ref-348" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-348">&#91;348&#93;</a></sup> Old English<sup id="cite_ref-349" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-349">&#91;349&#93;</a></sup> and French.<sup id="cite_ref-350" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-350">&#91;350&#93;</a></sup> The first surviving major text in <a href="/wiki/Early_Scots" title="Early Scots">Early Scots</a> is the 14th-century poet <a href="/wiki/John_Barbour_(poet)" title="John Barbour (poet)">John Barbour</a>'s epic <i><a href="/wiki/The_Brus" title="The Brus">Brus</a></i>, focusing on the life of Robert I,<sup id="cite_ref-351" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-351">&#91;351&#93;</a></sup> and was soon followed by a series of vernacular romances and prose works.<sup id="cite_ref-Wormald1991pp60-7_352-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Wormald1991pp60-7-352">&#91;352&#93;</a></sup> In the 16th century, the crown's patronage helped the development of Scots drama and poetry,<sup id="cite_ref-Brownetalpp256-7_353-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Brownetalpp256-7-353">&#91;353&#93;</a></sup> but the accession of James VI to the English throne removed a major centre of literary patronage and Scots was sidelined as a literary language.<sup id="cite_ref-354" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-354">&#91;354&#93;</a></sup> Interest in Scots literature was revived in the 18th century by figures including <a href="/wiki/James_Macpherson" title="James Macpherson">James Macpherson</a>, whose <a href="/wiki/Ossian" title="Ossian">Ossian Cycle</a> made him the first Scottish poet to gain an international reputation and was a major influence on the European Enlightenment.<sup id="cite_ref-355" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-355">&#91;355&#93;</a></sup> It was also a major influence on <a href="/wiki/Robert_Burns" title="Robert Burns">Robert Burns</a>, whom many consider the national poet,<sup id="cite_ref-356" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-356">&#91;356&#93;</a></sup> and <a href="/wiki/Walter_Scott" title="Walter Scott">Walter Scott</a>, whose <a href="/wiki/Waverley_Novels" title="Waverley Novels">Waverley Novels</a> did much to define Scottish identity in the 19th century.<sup id="cite_ref-357" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-357">&#91;357&#93;</a></sup> Towards the end of the Victorian era a number of Scottish-born authors achieved international reputations as writers in English, including <a href="/wiki/Robert_Louis_Stevenson" title="Robert Louis Stevenson">Robert Louis Stevenson</a>, <a href="/wiki/Arthur_Conan_Doyle" title="Arthur Conan Doyle">Arthur Conan Doyle</a>, <a href="/wiki/J._M._Barrie" title="J. M. Barrie">J. M. Barrie</a> and <a href="/wiki/George_MacDonald" title="George MacDonald">George MacDonald</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-358" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-358">&#91;358&#93;</a></sup> In the 20th century the <a href="/wiki/Scottish_Renaissance" title="Scottish Renaissance">Scottish Renaissance</a> saw a surge of literary activity and attempts to reclaim the Scots language as a medium for serious literature.<sup id="cite_ref-VisitingArtsScotland_359-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-VisitingArtsScotland-359">&#91;359&#93;</a></sup> Members of the movement were followed by a new generation of post-war poets including <a href="/wiki/Edwin_Morgan_(poet)" title="Edwin Morgan (poet)">Edwin Morgan</a>, who would be appointed the first <a href="/wiki/Scots_Makar" class="mw-redirect" title="Scots Makar">Scots Makar</a> by the inaugural Scottish government in 2004.<sup id="cite_ref-360" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-360">&#91;360&#93;</a></sup> From the 1980s Scottish literature enjoyed another major revival, particularly associated with a group of writers including <a href="/wiki/Irvine_Welsh" title="Irvine Welsh">Irvine Welsh</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-VisitingArtsScotland_359-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-VisitingArtsScotland-359">&#91;359&#93;</a></sup> Scottish poets who emerged in the same period included <a href="/wiki/Carol_Ann_Duffy" title="Carol Ann Duffy">Carol Ann Duffy</a>, who, in May 2009, was the first Scot named the monarch's <a href="/wiki/Poet_Laureate" class="mw-redirect" title="Poet Laureate">Poet Laureate</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-361" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-361">&#91;361&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Celtic_connections">Celtic connections</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/Celtic_nations" title="Celtic nations">Celtic nations</a></div>
<p>As one of the <a href="/wiki/Celtic_nations" title="Celtic nations">Celtic nations</a>, Scotland and Scottish culture are represented at interceltic events at home and over the world. Scotland hosts several music festivals including <a href="/wiki/Celtic_Connections" title="Celtic Connections">Celtic Connections</a> (Glasgow), and the <a href="/wiki/Hebridean_Celtic_Festival" title="Hebridean Celtic Festival">Hebridean Celtic Festival</a> (Stornoway). Festivals celebrating Celtic culture, such as <a href="/wiki/Festival_Interceltique_de_Lorient" title="Festival Interceltique de Lorient">Festival Interceltique de Lorient</a> (<a href="/wiki/Brittany" title="Brittany">Brittany</a>), the <a href="/wiki/Pan_Celtic_Festival" title="Pan Celtic Festival">Pan Celtic Festival</a> (Ireland), and the National Celtic Festival (<a href="/wiki/Portarlington,_Victoria" title="Portarlington, Victoria">Portarlington</a>, Australia), feature elements of Scottish culture such as language, music and dance.<sup id="cite_ref-Celtic_connections_1_362-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Celtic_connections_1-362">&#91;362&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Festival_1_363-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Festival_1-363">&#91;363&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Dingle_1_364-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Dingle_1-364">&#91;364&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-Festival_3_365-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Festival_3-365">&#91;365&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="National_identity">National identity</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Further information: <a href="/wiki/Scottish_people" title="Scottish people">Scottish people</a> and <a href="/wiki/National_symbols_of_Scotland" title="National symbols of Scotland">National symbols of Scotland</a></div>
<div class="thumb tleft"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:172px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Royal_Arms_of_the_Kingdom_of_Scotland.svg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bd/Royal_Arms_of_the_Kingdom_of_Scotland.svg/170px-Royal_Arms_of_the_Kingdom_of_Scotland.svg.png" decoding="async" width="170" height="199" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bd/Royal_Arms_of_the_Kingdom_of_Scotland.svg/255px-Royal_Arms_of_the_Kingdom_of_Scotland.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bd/Royal_Arms_of_the_Kingdom_of_Scotland.svg/340px-Royal_Arms_of_the_Kingdom_of_Scotland.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="512" data-file-height="599" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Royal_Arms_of_the_Kingdom_of_Scotland.svg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>The <a href="/wiki/Royal_arms_of_Scotland" title="Royal arms of Scotland">royal arms of Scotland</a></div></div></div>
<p>The image of <a href="/wiki/Saint_Andrew" class="mw-redirect" title="Saint Andrew">St. Andrew</a>, martyred while bound to an X-shaped cross, first appeared in the <a href="/wiki/Kingdom_of_Scotland" title="Kingdom of Scotland">Kingdom of Scotland</a> during the reign of <a href="/wiki/William_the_Lion" title="William the Lion">William I</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-NAS_366-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-NAS-366">&#91;366&#93;</a></sup> Following the death of <a href="/wiki/Alexander_III_of_Scotland" title="Alexander III of Scotland">King Alexander III</a> in 1286 an image of Andrew was used on the <a href="/wiki/Seal_(emblem)" title="Seal (emblem)">seal</a> of the <a href="/wiki/Guardians_of_Scotland" class="mw-redirect" title="Guardians of Scotland">Guardians of Scotland</a> who assumed control of the kingdom during the subsequent <a href="/wiki/Interregnum" title="Interregnum">interregnum</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-autogenerated2_367-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-autogenerated2-367">&#91;367&#93;</a></sup> Use of a simplified symbol associated with Saint Andrew, the <a href="/wiki/Saltire" title="Saltire">saltire</a>, has its origins in the late 14th century; the <a href="/wiki/Parliament_of_Scotland" title="Parliament of Scotland">Parliament of Scotland</a> decreeing in 1385 that Scottish soldiers should wear a white Saint Andrew's Cross on the front and back of their tunics.<sup id="cite_ref-368" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-368">&#91;368&#93;</a></sup> Use of a blue background for the Saint Andrew's Cross is said to date from at least the 15th century.<sup id="cite_ref-369" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-369">&#91;369&#93;</a></sup> Since 1606 the saltire has also formed part of the design of the <a href="/wiki/Union_Flag" class="mw-redirect" title="Union Flag">Union Flag</a>. There are numerous other symbols and symbolic artefacts, both official and unofficial, including the <a href="/wiki/Thistle" title="Thistle">thistle</a>, the nation's <a href="/wiki/National_emblem" title="National emblem">floral emblem</a> (celebrated in the song, <a href="/wiki/The_Thistle_o%27_Scotland" title="The Thistle o&#39; Scotland">The Thistle o' Scotland</a>), the <a href="/wiki/Declaration_of_Arbroath" title="Declaration of Arbroath">Declaration of Arbroath</a>, incorporating a statement of political independence made on 6 April 1320, the textile pattern <a href="/wiki/Tartan" title="Tartan">tartan</a> that often signifies a particular <a href="/wiki/Scottish_clan" title="Scottish clan">Scottish clan</a> and the royal <a href="/wiki/Royal_Standard_of_Scotland" class="mw-redirect" title="Royal Standard of Scotland">Lion Rampant</a> flag.<sup id="cite_ref-370" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-370">&#91;370&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-371" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-371">&#91;371&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-372" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-372">&#91;372&#93;</a></sup> Highlanders can thank <a href="/wiki/James_Graham,_3rd_Duke_of_Montrose" title="James Graham, 3rd Duke of Montrose">James Graham, 3rd Duke of Montrose</a>, for the repeal in 1782 of the Act of 1747 prohibiting the wearing of tartans.<sup id="cite_ref-Works_373-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Works-373">&#91;373&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:172px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Scottish_Thistle_(Heraldry).svg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bc/Scottish_Thistle_%28Heraldry%29.svg/170px-Scottish_Thistle_%28Heraldry%29.svg.png" decoding="async" width="170" height="170" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bc/Scottish_Thistle_%28Heraldry%29.svg/255px-Scottish_Thistle_%28Heraldry%29.svg.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/bc/Scottish_Thistle_%28Heraldry%29.svg/340px-Scottish_Thistle_%28Heraldry%29.svg.png 2x" data-file-width="250" data-file-height="250" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Scottish_Thistle_(Heraldry).svg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>The <a href="/wiki/Thistle" title="Thistle">thistle</a>, the <a href="/wiki/National_emblem" title="National emblem">national emblem</a> of Scotland</div></div></div>
<p>Although there is no official <a href="/wiki/National_anthem_of_Scotland" title="National anthem of Scotland">national anthem of Scotland</a>,<sup id="cite_ref-374" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-374">&#91;374&#93;</a></sup> <i><a href="/wiki/Flower_of_Scotland" title="Flower of Scotland">Flower of Scotland</a></i> is played on special occasions and sporting events such as football and rugby matches involving the Scotland national teams and since 2010 is also played at the Commonwealth Games after it was voted the overwhelming favourite by participating Scottish athletes.<sup id="cite_ref-375" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-375">&#91;375&#93;</a></sup> Other currently less popular candidates for the National Anthem of Scotland include <i><a href="/wiki/Scotland_the_Brave" title="Scotland the Brave">Scotland the Brave</a></i>, <i><a href="/wiki/Highland_Cathedral" title="Highland Cathedral">Highland Cathedral</a></i>, <i><a href="/wiki/Scots_Wha_Hae" title="Scots Wha Hae">Scots Wha Hae</a></i> and <i><a href="/wiki/A_Man%27s_A_Man_for_A%27_That" title="A Man&#39;s A Man for A&#39; That">A Man's A Man for A' That</a></i>.<sup id="cite_ref-376" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-376">&#91;376&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p><a href="/wiki/St_Andrew%27s_Day" class="mw-redirect" title="St Andrew&#39;s Day">St Andrew's Day</a>, 30 November, is the <a href="/wiki/National_day" title="National day">national day</a>, although <a href="/wiki/Burns%27_Night" class="mw-redirect" title="Burns&#39; Night">Burns' Night</a> tends to be more widely observed, particularly outside Scotland. In 2006, the Scottish Parliament passed the <a href="/wiki/St_Andrew%27s_Day_Bank_Holiday_(Scotland)_Act_2007" title="St Andrew&#39;s Day Bank Holiday (Scotland) Act 2007">St Andrew's Day Bank Holiday (Scotland) Act 2007</a>, designating the day an official <a href="/wiki/Bank_holiday" title="Bank holiday">bank holiday</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-377" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-377">&#91;377&#93;</a></sup> <a href="/wiki/Tartan_Day" title="Tartan Day">Tartan Day</a> is a recent innovation from Canada.<sup id="cite_ref-378" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-378">&#91;378&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The national animal of Scotland is the <a href="/wiki/Unicorn" title="Unicorn">unicorn</a>, which has been a Scottish heraldic symbol since the 12th century.<sup id="cite_ref-379" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-379">&#91;379&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Cuisine">Cuisine</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Scottish_cuisine" title="Scottish cuisine">Scottish cuisine</a></div>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Cock-a-leekie_Soup.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/80/Cock-a-leekie_Soup.jpg/220px-Cock-a-leekie_Soup.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/80/Cock-a-leekie_Soup.jpg/330px-Cock-a-leekie_Soup.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/80/Cock-a-leekie_Soup.jpg/440px-Cock-a-leekie_Soup.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2288" data-file-height="1712" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Cock-a-leekie_Soup.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div><a href="/wiki/Cock-a-leekie_soup" class="mw-redirect" title="Cock-a-leekie soup">Cock-a-leekie soup</a></div></div></div>
<p>Scottish cuisine has distinctive attributes and recipes of its own but shares much with wider <a href="/wiki/British_cuisine" title="British cuisine">British</a> and <a href="/wiki/European_cuisine" title="European cuisine">European cuisine</a> as a result of local and foreign influences, both ancient and modern. Traditional Scottish dishes exist alongside international foodstuffs brought about by migration. Scotland's natural larder of <a href="/wiki/Game_(food)" class="mw-redirect" title="Game (food)">game</a>, dairy products, fish, fruit, and vegetables is the chief factor in traditional Scots cooking, with a high reliance on simplicity and a lack of <a href="/wiki/Spice" title="Spice">spices</a> from abroad, as these were historically rare and expensive. <a href="/wiki/Irn-Bru" title="Irn-Bru">Irn-Bru</a> is the most common Scottish carbonated soft drink, often described as "Scotland's other national drink" (after whisky).<sup id="cite_ref-380" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-380">&#91;380&#93;</a></sup> During the <a href="/wiki/Late_Middle_Ages" title="Late Middle Ages">Late Middle Ages</a> and <a href="/wiki/Early_modern_era" class="mw-redirect" title="Early modern era">early modern era</a>, <a href="/wiki/French_cuisine" title="French cuisine">French cuisine</a> played a role in Scottish cookery due to cultural exchanges brought about by the "<a href="/wiki/Auld_Alliance" title="Auld Alliance">Auld Alliance</a>",<sup id="cite_ref-381" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-381">&#91;381&#93;</a></sup> especially during the reign of <a href="/wiki/Mary,_Queen_of_Scots" title="Mary, Queen of Scots">Mary, Queen of Scots</a>. Mary, on her return to Scotland, brought an entourage of French staff who are considered responsible for revolutionising Scots cooking and for some of Scotland's unique food terminology.<sup id="cite_ref-382" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-382">&#91;382&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Media">Media</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Media_of_Scotland" title="Media of Scotland">Media of Scotland</a></div>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:172px;"><a href="/wiki/File:John_Logie_Baird_in_1917.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/80/John_Logie_Baird_in_1917.jpg/170px-John_Logie_Baird_in_1917.jpg" decoding="async" width="170" height="234" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/80/John_Logie_Baird_in_1917.jpg/255px-John_Logie_Baird_in_1917.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/8/80/John_Logie_Baird_in_1917.jpg/340px-John_Logie_Baird_in_1917.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3918" data-file-height="5397" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:John_Logie_Baird_in_1917.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>Scottish inventor <a href="/wiki/John_Logie_Baird" title="John Logie Baird">John Logie Baird</a> demonstrated the first working television system on 26 January 1926.<sup id="cite_ref-383" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-383">&#91;383&#93;</a></sup></div></div></div>
<p>National newspapers such as the <a href="/wiki/Daily_Record_(Scotland)" title="Daily Record (Scotland)"><i>Daily Record</i></a>, <a href="/wiki/The_Herald_(Glasgow)" title="The Herald (Glasgow)"><i>The Herald</i></a>, <i><a href="/wiki/The_Scotsman" title="The Scotsman">The Scotsman</a></i> and <i><a href="/wiki/The_National_(Scotland)" title="The National (Scotland)">The National</a></i> are all produced in Scotland.<sup id="cite_ref-Newspapers_384-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Newspapers-384">&#91;384&#93;</a></sup> Important regional dailies include the <a href="/wiki/Edinburgh_Evening_News" title="Edinburgh Evening News">Evening News</a> in Edinburgh, <i><a href="/wiki/The_Courier_(Dundee)" title="The Courier (Dundee)">The Courier</a></i> in Dundee in the east, and <i><a href="/wiki/The_Press_and_Journal_(Scotland)" title="The Press and Journal (Scotland)">The Press and Journal</a></i> serving Aberdeen and the north.<sup id="cite_ref-Newspapers_384-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Newspapers-384">&#91;384&#93;</a></sup> Scotland is represented at the <a href="/wiki/Celtic_Media_Festival" title="Celtic Media Festival">Celtic Media Festival</a>, which showcases film and television from the Celtic countries. Scottish entrants have won many awards since the festival began in 1980.<sup id="cite_ref-Media_1_385-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Media_1-385">&#91;385&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Television in Scotland is largely the same as UK-wide broadcasts. The national broadcaster is <a href="/wiki/BBC_Scotland" title="BBC Scotland">BBC Scotland</a>, a division of the <a href="/wiki/BBC" title="BBC">BBC</a>. It runs three national <a href="/wiki/Scottish_television_stations" class="mw-redirect" title="Scottish television stations">television stations</a> <a href="/wiki/BBC_One_Scotland" title="BBC One Scotland">BBC One Scotland</a>, <a href="/wiki/BBC_Scotland_(TV_channel)" title="BBC Scotland (TV channel)">BBC Scotland channel</a> and the Gaelic-language broadcaster <a href="/wiki/BBC_Alba" title="BBC Alba">BBC Alba</a>, and the national radio stations, <i><a href="/wiki/BBC_Radio_Scotland" title="BBC Radio Scotland">BBC Radio Scotland</a></i> and <i><a href="/wiki/BBC_Radio_nan_G%C3%A0idheal" title="BBC Radio nan Gàidheal">BBC Radio nan Gàidheal</a></i>, amongst others. The main Scottish commercial television station is <a href="/wiki/STV_(TV_network)" class="mw-redirect" title="STV (TV network)">STV</a> which broadcasts on two of the three <a href="/wiki/ITV_(network)" class="mw-redirect" title="ITV (network)">ITV</a> regions of Scotland.<sup id="cite_ref-386" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-386">&#91;386&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<div class="thumb tleft"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:STV_HQ_%26_studios,_Pacific_Quay,_Glasgow_(geograph_3573858).jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4d/STV_HQ_%26_studios%2C_Pacific_Quay%2C_Glasgow_%28geograph_3573858%29.jpg/220px-STV_HQ_%26_studios%2C_Pacific_Quay%2C_Glasgow_%28geograph_3573858%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4d/STV_HQ_%26_studios%2C_Pacific_Quay%2C_Glasgow_%28geograph_3573858%29.jpg/330px-STV_HQ_%26_studios%2C_Pacific_Quay%2C_Glasgow_%28geograph_3573858%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/4/4d/STV_HQ_%26_studios%2C_Pacific_Quay%2C_Glasgow_%28geograph_3573858%29.jpg/440px-STV_HQ_%26_studios%2C_Pacific_Quay%2C_Glasgow_%28geograph_3573858%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="5184" data-file-height="3456" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:STV_HQ_%26_studios,_Pacific_Quay,_Glasgow_(geograph_3573858).jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div><a href="/wiki/STV_Group" title="STV Group">Scottish Television</a> (STV) HQ in Glasgow</div></div></div>
<p><a href="/wiki/List_of_Scotland-based_production_companies" title="List of Scotland-based production companies">Scotland has a number of production companies</a> which produce films and television programmes for Scottish, British and international audiences. Popular films associated with Scotland through Scottish production or being filmed in Scotland include <i><a href="/wiki/Braveheart_(film)" class="mw-redirect" title="Braveheart (film)">Braveheart</a></i> (1995),<sup id="cite_ref-scotland.org_387-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-scotland.org-387">&#91;387&#93;</a></sup> <i><a href="/wiki/Highlander_(film)" title="Highlander (film)">Highlander</a></i> (1986),<sup id="cite_ref-scotland.org_387-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-scotland.org-387">&#91;387&#93;</a></sup> <i><a href="/wiki/Trainspotting_(film)" title="Trainspotting (film)">Trainspotting</a></i> (1996),<sup id="cite_ref-scotland.org_387-2" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-scotland.org-387">&#91;387&#93;</a></sup> <i><a href="/wiki/Red_Road_(film)" title="Red Road (film)">Red Road</a></i> (2006), <i><a href="/wiki/Neds_(film)" title="Neds (film)">Neds</a></i> (2010),<sup id="cite_ref-scotland.org_387-3" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-scotland.org-387">&#91;387&#93;</a></sup> <i><a href="/wiki/The_Angel%27s_Share" class="mw-redirect" title="The Angel&#39;s Share">The Angel's Share</a></i> (2012), <i><a href="/wiki/Brave_(2012_film)" title="Brave (2012 film)">Brave</a></i> (2012)<sup id="cite_ref-388" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-388">&#91;388&#93;</a></sup> and <i><a href="/wiki/Outlaw_King" title="Outlaw King">Outlaw King</a></i> (2018).<sup id="cite_ref-389" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-389">&#91;389&#93;</a></sup> Popular television programmes associated with Scotland include the long running <a href="/wiki/BBC_Scotland" title="BBC Scotland">BBC Scotland</a> soap opera <i><a href="/wiki/River_City" title="River City">River City</a></i> which has been broadcast since 2002,<sup id="cite_ref-390" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-390">&#91;390&#93;</a></sup> <i><a href="/wiki/Still_Game" title="Still Game">Still Game</a></i>, a popular Scottish sitcom broadcast throughout the United Kingdom (2002–2007, revived in 2016),<sup id="cite_ref-391" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-391">&#91;391&#93;</a></sup> <i><a href="/wiki/Rab_C._Nesbitt" title="Rab C. Nesbitt">Rab C. Nesbitt</a></i>, <i><a href="/wiki/Two_Doors_Down_(TV_series)" title="Two Doors Down (TV series)">Two Doors Down</a></i><sup id="cite_ref-392" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-392">&#91;392&#93;</a></sup> and <i><a href="/wiki/Take_the_High_Road" title="Take the High Road">Take the High Road</a></i>.<sup id="cite_ref-393" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-393">&#91;393&#93;</a></sup> <i><a href="/wiki/The_Rig_(TV_series)" title="The Rig (TV series)">The Rig</a></i> (2023) was the first <a href="/wiki/Amazon_Prime_Video" title="Amazon Prime Video">Amazon Prime Video</a> production to be filmed and produced entirely in Scotland.<sup id="cite_ref-394" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-394">&#91;394&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Wardpark Studios in <a href="/wiki/Cumbernauld" title="Cumbernauld">Cumbernauld</a> is one of Scotland's television and film production studios where the television programme <i><a href="/wiki/Outlander_(TV_series)" title="Outlander (TV series)">Outlander</a></i> is produced.<sup id="cite_ref-395" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-395">&#91;395&#93;</a></sup> Dumbarton Studios, located in <a href="/wiki/Dumbarton" title="Dumbarton">Dumbarton</a> is largely used for <a href="/wiki/BBC_Scotland" title="BBC Scotland">BBC Scotland</a> programming, used for the filming and production of television programmes such as <i>Still Game</i>, <i>River City</i>, <i>Two Doors Down</i>, and <i><a href="/wiki/Shetland_(TV_series)" title="Shetland (TV series)">Shetland</a></i>.<sup id="cite_ref-396" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-396">&#91;396&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Sport">Sport</span></h2>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Sport_in_Scotland" title="Sport in Scotland">Sport in Scotland</a></div>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:322px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Hampden_Panorama.png" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b2/Hampden_Panorama.png/320px-Hampden_Panorama.png" decoding="async" width="320" height="75" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b2/Hampden_Panorama.png/480px-Hampden_Panorama.png 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b2/Hampden_Panorama.png/640px-Hampden_Panorama.png 2x" data-file-width="1200" data-file-height="280" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Hampden_Panorama.png" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div><a href="/wiki/Hampden_Park" title="Hampden Park">Hampden Park</a> is Scotland's national football stadium.</div></div></div>
<p>Scotland hosts its own national sporting competitions and has independent representation at several international sporting events, including the <a href="/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup" title="FIFA World Cup">FIFA World Cup</a>, the <a href="/wiki/UEFA_Nations_League" title="UEFA Nations League">UEFA Nations League</a>, the <a href="/wiki/UEFA_European_Championship" title="UEFA European Championship">UEFA European Championship</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Rugby_Union_World_Cup" class="mw-redirect" title="Rugby Union World Cup">Rugby Union World Cup</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Rugby_League_World_Cup" title="Rugby League World Cup">Rugby League World Cup</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Cricket_World_Cup" title="Cricket World Cup">Cricket World Cup</a>, the <a href="/wiki/Netball_World_Cup" title="Netball World Cup">Netball World Cup</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Commonwealth_Games" title="Commonwealth Games">Commonwealth Games</a>. Scotland has its own national governing bodies, such as the <a href="/wiki/Scottish_Football_Association" title="Scottish Football Association">Scottish Football Association</a> (the second oldest national football association in the world)<sup id="cite_ref-397" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-397">&#91;397&#93;</a></sup> and the <a href="/wiki/Scottish_Rugby_Union" title="Scottish Rugby Union">Scottish Rugby Union</a>. Variations of football have been played in Scotland for centuries, with the earliest reference dating back to 1424.<sup id="cite_ref-FIFA_398-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-FIFA-398">&#91;398&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Football">Football</span></h3>
<div class="thumb tleft"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:John_Fleck_and_Dmitriy_Barinov_(10.10.2019).jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/95/John_Fleck_and_Dmitriy_Barinov_%2810.10.2019%29.jpg/220px-John_Fleck_and_Dmitriy_Barinov_%2810.10.2019%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="147" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/95/John_Fleck_and_Dmitriy_Barinov_%2810.10.2019%29.jpg/330px-John_Fleck_and_Dmitriy_Barinov_%2810.10.2019%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/95/John_Fleck_and_Dmitriy_Barinov_%2810.10.2019%29.jpg/440px-John_Fleck_and_Dmitriy_Barinov_%2810.10.2019%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1800" data-file-height="1200" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:John_Fleck_and_Dmitriy_Barinov_(10.10.2019).jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div><a href="/wiki/Scotland_national_football_team" title="Scotland national football team">Scotland national football team</a> in competition against Russia, 2019</div></div></div>
<p>The world's first official international association football match was held in 1872 and was the idea of <a href="/wiki/C._W._Alcock" class="mw-redirect" title="C. W. Alcock">C. W. Alcock</a> of <a href="/wiki/The_Football_Association" title="The Football Association">the Football Association</a> which was seeking to promote <a href="/wiki/Association_Football" class="mw-redirect" title="Association Football">Association Football</a> in Scotland.<sup id="cite_ref-399" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-399">&#91;399&#93;</a></sup><sup class="noprint Inline-Template noprint noexcerpt Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:NOTRS" class="mw-redirect" title="Wikipedia:NOTRS"><span title="This claim needs references to better sources. (January 2019)">better&#160;source&#160;needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup> The match took place at the <a href="/wiki/West_of_Scotland_Cricket_Club" title="West of Scotland Cricket Club">West of Scotland Cricket Club</a>'s <a href="/wiki/Hamilton_Crescent" title="Hamilton Crescent">Hamilton Crescent</a> ground in the <a href="/wiki/Partick" title="Partick">Partick</a> area of <a href="/wiki/Glasgow" title="Glasgow">Glasgow</a>. The match was between <a href="/wiki/Scotland_national_football_team" title="Scotland national football team">Scotland</a> and <a href="/wiki/England_national_football_team" title="England national football team">England</a> and resulted in a 0–0 draw. Following this, the newly developed football became the most popular sport in Scotland. The <a href="/wiki/Scottish_Cup" title="Scottish Cup">Scottish Cup</a> was first contested in 1873. <a href="/wiki/Queen%27s_Park_F.C." title="Queen&#39;s Park F.C.">Queen's Park F.C.</a>, in Glasgow, is probably the oldest association football club in the world outside England.<sup id="cite_ref-400" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-400">&#91;400&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-401" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-401">&#91;401&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/Scottish_Football_Association" title="Scottish Football Association">Scottish Football Association</a> (SFA), the second-oldest national football association in the world, is the main <a href="/wiki/Sport_governing_body" class="mw-redirect" title="Sport governing body">governing body</a> for Scottish association football, and a founding member of the <a href="/wiki/International_Football_Association_Board" title="International Football Association Board">International Football Association Board</a> (IFAB) which governs the <a href="/wiki/Laws_of_the_Game_(association_football)" title="Laws of the Game (association football)">Laws of the Game</a>. As a result of this key role in the development of the sport Scotland is one of only four countries to have a permanent representative on the IFAB; the other four representatives being appointed for set periods by <a href="/wiki/FIFA" title="FIFA">FIFA</a>.<sup class="noprint Inline-Template Template-Fact" style="white-space:nowrap;">&#91;<i><a href="/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation_needed" title="Wikipedia:Citation needed"><span title="This claim needs references to reliable sources. (January 2019)">citation needed</span></a></i>&#93;</sup><sup id="cite_ref-402" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-402">&#91;402&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The SFA also has responsibility for the <a href="/wiki/Scotland_national_football_team" title="Scotland national football team">Scotland national football team</a>, whose supporters are commonly known as the "<a href="/wiki/Tartan_Army" title="Tartan Army">Tartan Army</a>". As of December 2019<sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><a class="external text" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Scotland&amp;action=edit">&#91;update&#93;</a></sup>, Scotland are ranked as the 50th best <a href="/wiki/List_of_men%27s_national_football_teams" class="mw-redirect" title="List of men&#39;s national football teams">national football team</a> in the <a href="/wiki/FIFA_World_Rankings" class="mw-redirect" title="FIFA World Rankings">FIFA World Rankings</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-403" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-403">&#91;403&#93;</a></sup> The national team last attended the <a href="/wiki/FIFA_World_Cup" title="FIFA World Cup">World Cup</a> in <a href="/wiki/1998_FIFA_World_Cup" title="1998 FIFA World Cup">France in 1998</a>, but finished last in their group stage.<sup id="cite_ref-404" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-404">&#91;404&#93;</a></sup> The <a href="/wiki/Scotland_women%27s_national_football_team" title="Scotland women&#39;s national football team">Scotland women's team</a> have achieved more recent success, qualifying for both <a href="/wiki/UEFA_Women%27s_Euro_2017" title="UEFA Women&#39;s Euro 2017">Euro 2017</a><sup id="cite_ref-405" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-405">&#91;405&#93;</a></sup> and the <a href="/wiki/2019_FIFA_Women%27s_World_Cup" title="2019 FIFA Women&#39;s World Cup">2019 World Cup</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-406" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-406">&#91;406&#93;</a></sup> As of December 2019<sup class="plainlinks noexcerpt noprint asof-tag update" style="display:none;"><a class="external text" href="https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=Scotland&amp;action=edit">&#91;update&#93;</a></sup>, they were ranked as the 22nd best <a href="/wiki/List_of_women%27s_national_football_teams" class="mw-redirect" title="List of women&#39;s national football teams">women's national team</a> in the <a href="/wiki/FIFA_Women%27s_World_Rankings" title="FIFA Women&#39;s World Rankings">FIFA Rankings</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-407" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-407">&#91;407&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Scottish clubs have achieved some success in European competitions, with <a href="/wiki/Celtic_F.C." title="Celtic F.C.">Celtic</a> winning the <a href="/wiki/European_Champion_Clubs%27_Cup" title="European Champion Clubs&#39; Cup">European Cup</a> in 1967, <a href="/wiki/Rangers_F.C." title="Rangers F.C.">Rangers</a> and <a href="/wiki/Aberdeen_F.C." title="Aberdeen F.C.">Aberdeen</a> winning the <a href="/wiki/UEFA_Cup_Winners%27_Cup" title="UEFA Cup Winners&#39; Cup">UEFA Cup Winners' Cup</a> in 1972 and 1983 respectively, and Aberdeen also winning the <a href="/wiki/UEFA_Super_Cup" title="UEFA Super Cup">UEFA Super Cup</a> in 1983. Celtic, Rangers and <a href="/wiki/Dundee_United_F.C." title="Dundee United F.C.">Dundee United</a> have also reached European finals. The most recent appearance by a Scottish club in a European final was by Rangers in <a href="/wiki/2022_UEFA_Europa_League_Final" class="mw-redirect" title="2022 UEFA Europa League Final">2022</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-408" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-408">&#91;408&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-409" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-409">&#91;409&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Golf">Golf</span></h3>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Old_18th_tee_lr.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/92/Old_18th_tee_lr.jpg/220px-Old_18th_tee_lr.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="146" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/92/Old_18th_tee_lr.jpg/330px-Old_18th_tee_lr.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/92/Old_18th_tee_lr.jpg/440px-Old_18th_tee_lr.jpg 2x" data-file-width="1393" data-file-height="925" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Old_18th_tee_lr.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>The <a href="/wiki/Old_Course_at_St_Andrews" title="Old Course at St Andrews">Old Course at St Andrews</a> where <a href="/wiki/Golf" title="Golf">golf</a> originates from</div></div></div>
<p>With the modern game of <a href="/wiki/Golf" title="Golf">golf</a> originating in 15th-century Scotland, the country is promoted as the <a href="/wiki/Golf_in_Scotland" title="Golf in Scotland">home of golf</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-410" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-410">&#91;410&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-411" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-411">&#91;411&#93;</a></sup><sup id="cite_ref-412" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-412">&#91;412&#93;</a></sup> To many golfers the <a href="/wiki/Old_Course_at_St_Andrews" title="Old Course at St Andrews">Old Course</a> in the Fife town of <a href="/wiki/St_Andrews" title="St Andrews">St Andrews</a>, an ancient <a href="/wiki/Links_(golf)" title="Links (golf)">links</a> course dating to before 1552,<sup id="cite_ref-413" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-413">&#91;413&#93;</a></sup> is considered a site of pilgrimage.<sup id="cite_ref-414" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-414">&#91;414&#93;</a></sup> In 1764, the standard 18-hole golf course was created at St Andrews when members modified the course from 22 to 18 holes.<sup id="cite_ref-415" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-415">&#91;415&#93;</a></sup> The world's oldest golf tournament, and golf's first major, is <a href="/wiki/The_Open_Championship" title="The Open Championship">The Open Championship</a>, which was first played on 17 October 1860 at Prestwick Golf Club, in Ayrshire, Scotland, with <a href="/wiki/Men%27s_major_golf_championships#Major_championship_winners" title="Men&#39;s major golf championships">Scottish golfers winning the earliest majors</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-416" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-416">&#91;416&#93;</a></sup> There are many other famous <a href="/wiki/Golf_in_Scotland" title="Golf in Scotland">golf courses in Scotland</a>, including <a href="/wiki/Carnoustie_Golf_Links" title="Carnoustie Golf Links">Carnoustie</a>, <a href="/wiki/Gleneagles_(Scotland)" title="Gleneagles (Scotland)">Gleneagles</a>, <a href="/wiki/Muirfield" title="Muirfield">Muirfield</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Royal_Troon" class="mw-redirect" title="Royal Troon">Royal Troon</a>.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Rugby">Rugby</span></h3>
<p>The Scottish Football Union was founded on Monday 3 March 1873 at a meeting held at <a href="/wiki/Glasgow_Academy" class="mw-redirect" title="Glasgow Academy">Glasgow Academy</a>, Elmbank Street, Glasgow.<sup id="cite_ref-417" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-417">&#91;417&#93;</a></sup> The Scottish Rugby Union is the second oldest rugby union in the world. In 1924 the SFU changed its name to become the Scottish Rugby Union.<sup id="cite_ref-1925GS_418-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-1925GS-418">&#91;418&#93;</a></sup> International games were played at <a href="/wiki/Inverleith_Sports_Ground" title="Inverleith Sports Ground">Inverleith</a> from 1899 to 1925 when Murrayfield was opened.
</p><p>The SRU owns <a href="/wiki/Murrayfield_Stadium" title="Murrayfield Stadium">Murrayfield Stadium</a> which is the main home ground of the <a href="/wiki/Scotland_national_rugby_union_team" title="Scotland national rugby union team">Scottish national team</a>. Scotland is represented in rugby tournaments by the <a href="/wiki/Scotland_national_rugby_union_team" title="Scotland national rugby union team">Scotland national rugby union team</a>. As of 4 December 2022, Scotland are 7th in the <a href="/wiki/World_Rugby_Rankings" title="World Rugby Rankings">World Rugby Rankings</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-419" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-419">&#91;419&#93;</a></sup> The Scotland rugby team played <a href="/wiki/1871_Scotland_versus_England_rugby_union_match" title="1871 Scotland versus England rugby union match">their first official</a> <a href="/wiki/Test_match_(rugby_union)" title="Test match (rugby union)">test match</a>, winning 1–0 against England at <a href="/wiki/Raeburn_Place" title="Raeburn Place">Raeburn Place</a> in 1871. Scotland has competed in the <a href="/wiki/Six_Nations_Championship" title="Six Nations Championship">Six Nations</a> from the inaugural tournament in 1883, winning it 14 times outright—including the last Five Nations in <a href="/wiki/1999_Five_Nations_Championship" title="1999 Five Nations Championship">1999</a>—and sharing it another 8. The Rugby World Cup was introduced in 1987 and Scotland have competed in all nine competitions, the most recent being in <a href="/wiki/2019_Rugby_World_Cup" title="2019 Rugby World Cup">2019</a>, where they failed to reach the quarter-finals. Their best finish came in <a href="/wiki/1991_Rugby_World_Cup" title="1991 Rugby World Cup">1991</a>, where they lost to the <a href="/wiki/All_Blacks" class="mw-redirect" title="All Blacks">All Blacks</a> in the <a href="/wiki/Third_place_playoff" title="Third place playoff">third place play-off</a>.
</p><p>Scotland competes with the England rugby team annually for the <a href="/wiki/Calcutta_Cup" title="Calcutta Cup">Calcutta Cup</a>. Each year, this fixture is played out as part of the Six Nations, with Scotland having last won in 2022.
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Other_sports">Other sports</span></h3>
<p>Other distinctive features of the national sporting culture include the <a href="/wiki/Highland_games" title="Highland games">Highland games</a>, <a href="/wiki/Curling" title="Curling">curling</a> and <a href="/wiki/Shinty" title="Shinty">shinty</a>. In <a href="/wiki/Boxing" title="Boxing">boxing</a>, Scotland has had 13 world champions, including <a href="/wiki/Ken_Buchanan" title="Ken Buchanan">Ken Buchanan</a>, <a href="/wiki/Benny_Lynch" title="Benny Lynch">Benny Lynch</a> and <a href="/wiki/Jim_Watt_(boxer)" title="Jim Watt (boxer)">Jim Watt</a>. Scotland has also been successful in <a href="/wiki/Motorsport" title="Motorsport">motorsport</a>, particularly in <a href="/wiki/Formula_One" title="Formula One">Formula One</a>. Notable drivers include; <a href="/wiki/David_Coulthard" title="David Coulthard">David Coulthard</a>, <a href="/wiki/Jim_Clark" title="Jim Clark">Jim Clark</a>, <a href="/wiki/Paul_Di_Resta" class="mw-redirect" title="Paul Di Resta">Paul Di Resta</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Jackie_Stewart" title="Jackie Stewart">Jackie Stewart</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-420" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-420">&#91;420&#93;</a></sup> In <a href="/wiki/IndyCar_Series" title="IndyCar Series">IndyCar</a>, <a href="/wiki/Dario_Franchitti" title="Dario Franchitti">Dario Franchitti</a> has won 4 consecutive <a href="/wiki/IndyCar_Series" title="IndyCar Series">IndyCar world championships</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-421" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-421">&#91;421&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Scotland has competed at every Commonwealth Games since 1930 and has won 356 medals in total—91 Gold, 104 Silver and 161 Bronze.<sup id="cite_ref-422" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-422">&#91;422&#93;</a></sup> Edinburgh played host to the Commonwealth Games in <a href="/wiki/1970_British_Commonwealth_Games" title="1970 British Commonwealth Games">1970</a> and <a href="/wiki/1986_Commonwealth_Games" title="1986 Commonwealth Games">1986</a>, and most recently <a href="/wiki/Glasgow" title="Glasgow">Glasgow</a> in <a href="/wiki/2014_Commonwealth_Games" title="2014 Commonwealth Games">2014</a>.<sup id="cite_ref-423" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-423">&#91;423&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h2><span class="mw-headline" id="Infrastructure">Infrastructure</span></h2>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Energy">Energy</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">See also: <a href="/wiki/Nuclear_power_in_Scotland" title="Nuclear power in Scotland">Nuclear power in Scotland</a> and <a href="/wiki/Renewable_energy_in_Scotland" title="Renewable energy in Scotland">Renewable energy in Scotland</a></div>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Whitelee_Wind_Farm_(5284691105).jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d0/Whitelee_Wind_Farm_%285284691105%29.jpg/220px-Whitelee_Wind_Farm_%285284691105%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="157" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d0/Whitelee_Wind_Farm_%285284691105%29.jpg/330px-Whitelee_Wind_Farm_%285284691105%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d0/Whitelee_Wind_Farm_%285284691105%29.jpg/440px-Whitelee_Wind_Farm_%285284691105%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2100" data-file-height="1500" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Whitelee_Wind_Farm_(5284691105).jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div><a href="/wiki/Whitelee_Wind_Farm" title="Whitelee Wind Farm">Whitelee Wind Farm</a> is the largest onshore wind farm on the <a href="/wiki/British_Isles" title="British Isles">British Isles</a>.</div></div></div>
<p>Scotland's primary sources for energy are provided through renewable energy (61.8%), nuclear (25.7%) and fossil fuel generation (10.9%).<sup id="cite_ref-:10_424-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:10-424">&#91;424&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>In Scotland, 98.6% of all electricity used was from renewable sources. This is minus net exports.<sup id="cite_ref-:10_424-1" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-:10-424">&#91;424&#93;</a></sup> Between October 2021 and September 2022 63.1% of all electricity generated in Scotland was from renewable sources, 83.6% was classed as low carbon and 14.5% was from fossil fuels.<sup id="cite_ref-425" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-425">&#91;425&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The Scottish Government has a target to have the equivalent of 50% of the energy for Scotland's heat, transport and electricity consumption to be supplied from renewable sources by 2030.<sup id="cite_ref-426" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-426">&#91;426&#93;</a></sup>
</p>
<h3><span class="mw-headline" id="Transport">Transport</span></h3>
<link rel="mw-deduplicated-inline-style" href="mw-data:TemplateStyles:r1033289096"/><div role="note" class="hatnote navigation-not-searchable">Main article: <a href="/wiki/Transport_in_Scotland" title="Transport in Scotland">Transport in Scotland</a></div>
<h4><span class="mw-headline" id="Air">Air</span></h4>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Barra_Airport_Arrivals_(geograph_3230484).jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e2/Barra_Airport_Arrivals_%28geograph_3230484%29.jpg/220px-Barra_Airport_Arrivals_%28geograph_3230484%29.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e2/Barra_Airport_Arrivals_%28geograph_3230484%29.jpg/330px-Barra_Airport_Arrivals_%28geograph_3230484%29.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/e2/Barra_Airport_Arrivals_%28geograph_3230484%29.jpg/440px-Barra_Airport_Arrivals_%28geograph_3230484%29.jpg 2x" data-file-width="3648" data-file-height="2736" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Barra_Airport_Arrivals_(geograph_3230484).jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div><a href="/wiki/Barra_Airport" title="Barra Airport">Barra Airport</a>, the only airport in the world to use a <a href="/wiki/Tide" title="Tide">tidal</a> <a href="/wiki/Beach" title="Beach">beach</a> as the runway</div></div></div>
<p>Scotland has five international airports operating scheduled services to Europe, North America and Asia, as well as domestic services to England, Northern Ireland and Wales.
</p>
<ul><li><a href="/wiki/Aberdeen_Airport" title="Aberdeen Airport">Aberdeen Airport</a></li>
<li><a href="/wiki/Edinburgh_Airport" title="Edinburgh Airport">Edinburgh Airport</a></li>
<li><a href="/wiki/Glasgow_Airport" title="Glasgow Airport">Glasgow Airport</a></li>
<li><a href="/wiki/Glasgow_Prestwick_Airport" title="Glasgow Prestwick Airport">Glasgow Prestwick Airport</a></li>
<li><a href="/wiki/Inverness_Airport" title="Inverness Airport">Inverness Airport</a></li></ul>
<p><a href="/wiki/Highlands_and_Islands_Airports" title="Highlands and Islands Airports">Highlands and Islands Airports</a> operates eleven airports across the <a href="/wiki/Scottish_Highlands" title="Scottish Highlands">Highlands</a>, <a href="/wiki/Orkney" title="Orkney">Orkney</a>, <a href="/wiki/Shetland" title="Shetland">Shetland</a> and the <a href="/wiki/Western_Isles" class="mw-redirect" title="Western Isles">Western Isles</a>, which are primarily used for short distance, public service operations, although Inverness Airport has a number of scheduled flights to destinations across the UK and mainland Europe.
</p><p>Edinburgh Airport is currently Scotland's busiest airport handling over 13 million passengers in 2017.<sup id="cite_ref-427" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-427">&#91;427&#93;</a></sup> It is also the UK's 6th busiest airport.
</p><p><a href="/wiki/British_Airways" title="British Airways">British Airways</a>, <a href="/wiki/EasyJet" title="EasyJet">EasyJet</a>, <a href="/wiki/Jet2" class="mw-redirect" title="Jet2">Jet2</a>, and <a href="/wiki/Ryanair" title="Ryanair">Ryanair</a> operate the majority of flights between Scotland and other major UK and European airports.
</p><p>Four airlines are based in Scotland:
</p>
<ul><li><a href="/wiki/Directflight" title="Directflight">Directflight</a></li>
<li><a href="/wiki/Hebridean_Air_Services" title="Hebridean Air Services">Hebridean Air Services</a></li>
<li><a href="/wiki/Loch_Lomond_Seaplanes" title="Loch Lomond Seaplanes">Loch Lomond Seaplanes</a></li>
<li><a href="/wiki/Loganair" title="Loganair">Loganair</a></li></ul>
<h4><span class="mw-headline" id="Rail">Rail</span></h4>
<div class="thumb tleft"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Forth_bridge_evening_long_exposure.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9e/Forth_bridge_evening_long_exposure.jpg/220px-Forth_bridge_evening_long_exposure.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="146" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9e/Forth_bridge_evening_long_exposure.jpg/330px-Forth_bridge_evening_long_exposure.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/9/9e/Forth_bridge_evening_long_exposure.jpg/440px-Forth_bridge_evening_long_exposure.jpg 2x" data-file-width="4225" data-file-height="2806" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Forth_bridge_evening_long_exposure.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>The <a href="/wiki/Forth_Bridge" title="Forth Bridge">Forth Bridge</a> in Edinburgh, a well-known structure in Scottish rail and a <a href="/wiki/UNESCO_World_Heritage_Site" class="mw-redirect" title="UNESCO World Heritage Site">UNESCO World Heritage Site</a></div></div></div>
<p><a href="/wiki/Network_Rail" title="Network Rail">Network Rail</a> owns and operates the fixed infrastructure assets of the railway system in Scotland, while the Scottish Government retains overall responsibility for rail strategy and funding in Scotland.<sup id="cite_ref-Office_of_Rail_Regulation_428-0" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-Office_of_Rail_Regulation-428">&#91;428&#93;</a></sup> Scotland's rail network has 359 railway stations and around 1,710 miles (2,760&#160;km) of track.<sup id="cite_ref-429" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-429">&#91;429&#93;</a></sup> In 2018–19 there were 102<span class="nowrap">&#160;</span>million passenger journeys on Scottish railways.<sup id="cite_ref-430" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-430">&#91;430&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>The <a href="/wiki/East_Coast_Main_Line" title="East Coast Main Line">East</a> and <a href="/wiki/West_Coast_Main_Line" title="West Coast Main Line">West Coast Main Lines</a> are the two cross-border railways that connect the networks of Scotland and England. <a href="/wiki/London_North_Eastern_Railway" title="London North Eastern Railway">London North Eastern Railway</a> (LNER) provides inter-city rail journeys on the former between <a href="/wiki/Inverness_railway_station" title="Inverness railway station">Inverness</a>, <a href="/wiki/Aberdeen_railway_station" title="Aberdeen railway station">Aberdeen</a> and <a href="/wiki/Edinburgh" title="Edinburgh">Edinburgh</a> to <a href="/wiki/London_King%27s_Cross_railway_station" title="London King&#39;s Cross railway station">London King’s Cross</a> via <a href="/wiki/York_railway_station" title="York railway station">York</a>, while <a href="/wiki/Avanti_West_Coast" title="Avanti West Coast">Avanti West Coast</a> runs services on the latter from either <a href="/wiki/Edinburgh_Waverley_railway_station" title="Edinburgh Waverley railway station">Edinburgh</a> or <a href="/wiki/Glasgow_Central_station" class="mw-redirect" title="Glasgow Central station">Glasgow Central</a> to <a href="/wiki/Euston_railway_station" title="Euston railway station">London Euston</a> with some services serving <a href="/wiki/Birmingham_New_Street_railway_station" title="Birmingham New Street railway station">Birmingham New Street</a>. <a href="/wiki/TransPennine_Express" title="TransPennine Express">TransPennine Express</a>, <a href="/wiki/Lumo_(train_operating_company)" title="Lumo (train operating company)">Lumo</a>, <a href="/wiki/CrossCountry" title="CrossCountry">CrossCountry</a>, <a href="/wiki/Caledonian_Sleeper" title="Caledonian Sleeper">Caledonian Sleeper</a> and <a href="/wiki/ScotRail" title="ScotRail">ScotRail</a> also operate services to England. Domestic rail services within Scotland are operated by ScotRail. Glasgow’s <a href="/wiki/Glasgow_Subway" title="Glasgow Subway">Subway</a> is one of the four underground urban rail networks in the UK (the others being in <a href="/wiki/London_Underground" title="London Underground">London</a>, <a href="/wiki/Tyne_and_Wear_Metro" title="Tyne and Wear Metro">Newcastle</a> and <a href="/wiki/Merseyrail" title="Merseyrail">Liverpool</a>). Edinburgh has a <a href="/wiki/Edinburgh_Trams" title="Edinburgh Trams">tramway</a> to and from the airport.
</p>
<div class="thumb tright"><div class="thumbinner" style="width:222px;"><a href="/wiki/File:Glenfinnan_Viaduct.jpg" class="image"><img alt="" src="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/17/Glenfinnan_Viaduct.jpg/220px-Glenfinnan_Viaduct.jpg" decoding="async" width="220" height="165" class="thumbimage" srcset="//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/17/Glenfinnan_Viaduct.jpg/330px-Glenfinnan_Viaduct.jpg 1.5x, //upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/17/Glenfinnan_Viaduct.jpg/440px-Glenfinnan_Viaduct.jpg 2x" data-file-width="2304" data-file-height="1728" /></a>  <div class="thumbcaption"><div class="magnify"><a href="/wiki/File:Glenfinnan_Viaduct.jpg" class="internal" title="Enlarge"></a></div>The <a href="/wiki/Glenfinnan_Viaduct" title="Glenfinnan Viaduct">Glenfinnan Viaduct</a></div></div></div>
<p>During the time of <a href="/wiki/British_Rail" title="British Rail">British Rail</a>, the West Coast Main Line from <a href="/wiki/Euston_railway_station" title="Euston railway station">London Euston</a> to <a href="/wiki/Glasgow_Central_railway_station" title="Glasgow Central railway station">Glasgow Central</a> was electrified in the early 1970s, followed by the East Coast Main Line in the late 1980s. British Rail created the <a href="/wiki/ScotRail_(brand)" title="ScotRail (brand)">ScotRail brand</a>. When British Rail existed, many railway lines in Strathclyde were electrified. Strathclyde Passenger Transport Executive was at the forefront with the acclaimed "largest electrified rail network outside London". Some parts of the network are electrified, but there are no electrified lines in the Highlands, Angus, Aberdeenshire, the cities of Dundee or Aberdeen, or Perth &amp; Kinross, and none of the islands have a rail link. Trains serving railheads such as <a href="/wiki/Wemyss_Bay_railway_station" title="Wemyss Bay railway station">Wemyss Bay</a>, <a href="/wiki/Kyle_of_Lochalsh_railway_station" title="Kyle of Lochalsh railway station">Kyle of Lochalsh</a> and <a href="/wiki/Mallaig_railway_station" title="Mallaig railway station">Mallaig</a> are often timed to connect with ferries to some of Scotland’s islands.
</p>
<h4><span class="mw-headline" id="Road">Road</span></h4>
<p>The Scottish motorways and major <a href="/wiki/Trunk_roads" class="mw-redirect" title="Trunk roads">trunk roads</a> are managed by <a href="/wiki/Transport_Scotland" title="Transport Scotland">Transport Scotland</a>. The remainder of the road network is managed by the <a href="/wiki/Scottish_local_authorities" class="mw-redirect" title="Scottish local authorities">Scottish local authorities</a> in each of their areas.
</p>
<h4><span class="mw-headline" id="Water">Water</span></h4>
<p>Regular ferry services operate between the Scottish mainland and outlying islands. Ferries serving both the inner and outer <a href="/wiki/Hebrides" title="Hebrides">Hebrides</a> are principally operated by the <a href="/wiki/State-owned_enterprise" title="State-owned enterprise">state-owned enterprise</a> <a href="/wiki/Caledonian_MacBrayne" title="Caledonian MacBrayne">Caledonian MacBrayne</a>.
</p><p>Services to the <a href="/wiki/Northern_Isles" title="Northern Isles">Northern Isles</a> are operated by <a href="/wiki/Serco" title="Serco">Serco</a>. Other routes, served by multiple companies, connect southwest Scotland to <a href="/wiki/Northern_Ireland" title="Northern Ireland">Northern Ireland</a>. <a href="/wiki/DFDS_Seaways" title="DFDS Seaways">DFDS Seaways</a> operated a freight-only <a href="/wiki/Rosyth_%E2%80%93_Zeebrugge_ferry_service" title="Rosyth – Zeebrugge ferry service">Rosyth – Zeebrugge ferry service</a>, until a fire damaged the vessel DFDS were using.<sup id="cite_ref-431" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-431">&#91;431&#93;</a></sup> A passenger service was also operated between 2002 and 2010.<sup id="cite_ref-432" class="reference"><a href="#cite_note-432">&#91;432&#93;</a></sup>
</p><p>Additional routes are operated by local authorities.
</p>
